rounds_per_day.max: 36 holes (2 rounds) per day, only if group is under 50 and conditions allow
rounds_per_day.arrival_day: Never schedule 18 if flight lands after 10am. Suggest par-3, range, or putting contest instead.

tee_time_spacing.buffer: Always build in 30 min before tee time for range warm-up

travel_days.day_1: Travel + settle in. Casual 9-hole, putting contest, or par-3. Welcome dinner.
travel_days.last_day: Checkout + travel. No golf unless early morning round and late flight.
travel_days.airport_buffer: At least 3 hours between last putt and airport departure

housing_rules.large_groups: Groups of 8+: consider two adjacent houses over one mansion (bathroom ratio matters)
housing_rules.airbnb_vs_resort: Airbnb/VRBO is cheaper for 8+ people, every time. Resort is worth it for 4-6 or premium trips.
housing_rules.kitchen_savings: House with kitchen saves $15-20/person/day on breakfasts and casual meals

2_to_4.best_for: Bucket list trips, premium experiences, father-son, couples
2_to_4.logistics: Easy — one tee time, one dinner reservation

4_to_8.best_for: Most golf trips. Sweet spot for logistics and fun.
destinations: Any destination works well at this size
4_to_8.logistics: Manageable — 1-2 tee times, most restaurants handle this

8_to_12.best_for: The classic boys trip. Big enough for competition, small enough to manage.

12_to_16.best_for: Reunion trips, bachelor parties, corporate outings

destinations.avoid_reason: 115°F+ temps make afternoon rounds brutal.

top_courses.name: TPC Scottsdale (Champions Course)

top_courses.name: We-Ko-Pa (Saguaro Course)

top_courses.name: We-Ko-Pa (Cholla Course)

top_courses.name: Troon North (Monument Course)

hidden_gems.name: Papago Golf Course

hidden_gems.name: Lookout Mountain Golf Club

lodging_options.name: We-Ko-Pa Resort
lodging_options.note: On-site at We-Ko-Pa courses. Pool, restaurant, casino nearby. 25 min from Old Town.

lodging_options.name: Scottsdale Resort at McCormick Ranch
lodging_options.note: Central location, good pool scene, walking distance to restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Old Town Scottsdale house

dining.name: Dominick's Steakhouse

top_courses.name: Caledonia Golf & Fish Club

top_courses.name: True Blue Golf Club

top_courses.name: Barefoot Resort (Dye Course)

top_courses.name: Tidewater Golf Club

top_courses.name: Myrtle Beach National (King's North)
top_courses.must_know: The Gambler hole (#6) is a par-5 with island fairway. Arnold Palmer design, fun for all levels, great value.

hidden_gems.name: Thistle Golf Club

hidden_gems.name: Pawleys Plantation
hidden_gems.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design in Pawleys Island. Marsh views, less crowded.

lodging_options.name: Barefoot Resort

bonus_plays.name: Sea Captain's House

destinations.why_go: Golf by day, Vegas by night. Only destination where non-golf friends want to come. Great desert courses within 30 minutes of the Strip.

top_courses.name: Shadow Creek
top_courses.must_know: Best-conditioned course in America. Built by Steve Wynn at $60M. Limo picks you up from hotel. Must stay at MGM property.

top_courses.name: TPC Las Vegas
top_courses.must_know: Home of the Shriners Open. Solid PGA Tour venue. 20 min from the Strip.

top_courses.name: Wolf Creek Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: 90 min from Strip in Mesquite but WORTH IT. Most visually stunning course in America. Extreme elevation changes. Unplayable for beginners, unforgettable for everyone else.

top_courses.name: Paiute Golf Resort (Wolf Course)
top_courses.must_know: Three Pete Dye courses on one property. Wolf is the best and toughest. 25 min from Strip. Great value.

top_courses.name: Cascata
top_courses.must_know: Waterfall behind the clubhouse. Rees Jones design in Boulder City. Premium experience without the Shadow Creek price.

hidden_gems.name: Coyote Springs Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Nicklaus design 50 min from Strip. Massive development that stalled — incredible course at a fraction of what it should cost.

hidden_gems.name: Las Vegas Paiute (Snow Mountain)
hidden_gems.must_know: Most forgiving of the 3 Paiute courses. Good for mixed skill groups.

lodging_options.name: MGM Grand / Bellagio / Aria
lodging_options.note: Stay MGM property to access Shadow Creek. Strip location for nightlife.

lodging_options.name: Caesars Palace / Paris / Flamingo

lodging_options.name: Off-Strip house
lodging_options.note: 15 min from Strip. Pool + hot tub. Good for large groups who want a home base.

dining.name: In-N-Out Burger

top_courses.name: Maderas Golf Club

top_courses.name: Coronado Municipal Golf Course

hidden_gems.name: Steele Canyon (Ranch/Vineyard)
hidden_gems.must_know: 27 holes east of San Diego. Ranch and Vineyard nines are the best combo. Great value with mountain views.

hidden_gems.name: Barona Creek Golf Club

lodging_options.note: Luxury right at Torrey Pines. Priority tee times. Splurge option for small groups.

hidden_gems.name: Oyster Reef Golf Club

lodging_options.name: Palmetto Dunes Oceanfront Resort

Fly into SAV and drive 45 min — flights to HHH are limited and expensive
Spring (Apr-May) is ideal: azaleas blooming, warm but not brutal, Heritage week energy
Bluffton (10 min away) has great restaurants and less tourist markup

items.title: Arrive SAV, drive to Sea Pines

destinations.kit_tagline: Play Harbour Town's lighthouse finish, bike Sea Pines paths, and skip the Myrtle Beach crowds for actual Lowcountry charm.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-April hits peak azalea bloom, avoids Heritage week crowds, and delivers warm weather without summer humidity.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: SAV arrival leaves time for lunch stop and check-in, then warm-up round on forgiving fairways at value pricing.
Afternoon light hits the lighthouse perfectly at 18, and you avoid morning dew on Pete Dye's tight tree-lined corridors.
Morning round before heat builds, then full afternoon free for beach or bikes through Sea Pines.
Best of the three Palmetto Dunes tracks, early enough to finish by noon and leave afternoon open for dolphin cruise or rest.
Checkout and 45-minute drive to SAV with buffer for afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Sea Pines Resort (villas)
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Only way to access Harbour Town, which is the entire point of HHH. Villas sleep 6-8, bike paths everywhere, and you're inside the gate for Atlantic Dunes too.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 60+ days out during spring, especially April-May when Heritage energy lingers.

bonus_plays.name: Skull Creek Boathouse
bonus_plays.why: Request the deck for sunset over the marsh. Raw bar is legit and the she-crab soup does the Lowcountry right.

bonus_plays.name: Quarterdeck at Harbour Town
bonus_plays.why: Post-Harbour Town beers at the marina. Watch boats come in and decompress the #18 lighthouse stories.

bonus_plays.name: Old South Golf Links
bonus_plays.why: In Bluffton, 15 minutes off island. If you want a fifth round on Day 4 afternoon, it's $50-75 with marsh views and no resort markup.

bonus_plays.name: One Hot Mama's
bonus_plays.why: Best ribs on the island, big portions, zero pretense. The group dinner that doesn't need a reservation.

destinations.nearest_airport: MRY (Monterey) or SJC (San Jose) or SFO
destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 10 min from MRY, 75 min from SJC, 2 hrs from SFO
destinations.avoid_reason: Rainy season. Course is open but cold, wet, and often foggy. You're paying $600+ — you want sun.
destinations.why_go: The #1 public course in America. If you play golf, you have to play Pebble Beach at least once. The coastline on holes 6-10 is the most beautiful stretch in golf.

top_courses.name: Pebble Beach Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: Must stay at Pebble Beach Resorts property for guaranteed tee time. Walk-on possible but rare. Caddie recommended ($75 + tip). #7 par-3 is 106 yards of pure adrenaline.

top_courses.name: Spyglass Hill
top_courses.must_know: Harder than Pebble. Front 9 is dunes/ocean, back 9 is forest. Robert Trent Jones Sr. Many say it's the better golf course (just not the views).

top_courses.name: The Links at Spanish Bay
top_courses.must_know: Scottish links-style on the ocean. Bagpiper plays at sunset from the Inn. The most atmospheric course on the peninsula.
top_courses.designer: Robert Trent Jones Jr., Tom Watson, Sandy Tatum

top_courses.name: Pacific Grove Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: The 'poor man's Pebble Beach.' Municipal course with ocean views and deer on the fairways. Back 9 along the coast is surprisingly beautiful. Best $55 you'll spend.

hidden_gems.name: Bayonet & Black Horse (Bayonet)
hidden_gems.must_know: Former military course in Seaside. Brutally hard but great conditions and ocean views for a fraction of Pebble.

hidden_gems.name: Pasadera Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Nicklaus design. Semi-private but public access available. Excellent conditions.

lodging_options.name: The Lodge at Pebble Beach
lodging_options.note: Guaranteed Pebble tee time. The ultimate. 2-person rooms only.

lodging_options.name: The Inn at Spanish Bay
lodging_options.note: On-site at Spanish Bay. Sunset bagpiper. Also gets Pebble tee times.

lodging_options.name: Monterey hotels (Portola, Marriott)
lodging_options.note: 10-15 min from Pebble. Can try for public tee times. Much cheaper.

lodging_options.name: Pacific Grove cottage
lodging_options.note: Charming town. Walk to Pacific Grove muni. No guaranteed Pebble tee times.

dining.name: The Bench (Pebble Beach)
dining.group_note: At The Lodge, overlooking #18 green. The celebration meal.

dining.name: Roy's at Spanish Bay
dining.group_note: Great food, ocean views, more relaxed than The Bench.

dining.name: Fisherman's Wharf (Monterey)
dining.group_note: Classic clam chowder in a bread bowl. Tourist spot but fun.

dining.name: Montrio Bistro
dining.group_note: Downtown Monterey. Great cocktails, creative menu. Reserve for groups.

insider_tips: Stay at an on-site resort to guarantee Pebble Beach tee times — it's the only reliable way
Pair Pebble + Spyglass for consecutive days. Spanish Bay on arrival day (links, no pressure)
Play Pacific Grove muni the evening before Pebble — it's $55 with ocean views and gets you calibrated
Walk Pebble with a caddie — riding dilutes the experience. Your caddie will be incredible
Afternoon fog is common Jun-Aug (the 'June Gloom'). Morning tee times have better chance of sun
17-Mile Drive is free if you're going to a Pebble Beach resort — save the $11.25 entrance fee
This trip works best as a foursome. It's too expensive for 8+ unless everyone is committed

items.title: Arrive MRY, drive to The Inn at Spanish Bay
Monterey Bay Aquarium or wine tasting

destinations.kit_tagline: Play the #1 public course in America, walk holes 6-10 along the cliffs, and check the box you've been thinking about for years.

default_recommended_dates.reason: September avoids June Gloom fog, catches warmer temps, and misses summer peak pricing.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival day with links golf — no pressure, atmospheric, and you'll catch the sunset bagpiper after.
Morning tee time beats afternoon fog and gives you the best light on holes 7-10. Walk it with a caddie.
Harder than Pebble — play it when you're still sharp. Front 9 ocean views, back 9 forest elevation changes.
Checkout and travel home. If you have a late flight, play Pacific Grove muni for $55 and ocean views.

recommended_lodging.name: The Inn at Spanish Bay
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Guarantees your Pebble tee time, puts you on-site at Spanish Bay for day 1, and the sunset bagpiper is part of the experience. You're already spending this much on golf — sleep where it matters.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 90+ days out. Pebble tee times are locked to resort stays.

bonus_plays.name: Pacific Grove Golf Links
bonus_plays.why: Play it the evening before Pebble — it's $55, has ocean views on the back 9, and gets you calibrated without pressure.
bonus_plays.when: Day 1 evening or Day 4 morning if late flight

bonus_plays.name: The Bench at Pebble Beach
bonus_plays.why: Overlooks the 18th green. Book it for the night after you play Pebble — you'll want to relive every shot.

bonus_plays.name: Sunset bagpiper at Spanish Bay
bonus_plays.why: Happens every evening at sunset. Stand on the patio with a drink and watch the piper walk the dunes. It's free and unforgettable.

bonus_plays.name: Montrio Bistro
bonus_plays.why: Downtown Monterey with creative menu and strong cocktails. More relaxed than resort dining and easier to get a table for four.

destinations.avoid_reason: Peak heat, humidity, and hurricane season. Bugs are intense.
destinations.why_go: The Ocean Course is a top-10 course in America and hosted the 2021 PGA Championship. Five courses on one island with world-class resort amenities. Add Charleston's food scene 45 min away.

top_courses.name: The Ocean Course
top_courses.must_know: Every hole has ocean views — only course in the US where this is true. Wind is ALWAYS a factor. Site of the 1991 Ryder Cup 'War by the Shore' and 2021 PGA Championship. Caddie mandatory.

top_courses.name: Osprey Point
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design through marshes and lagoons. Most playable Kiawah course. Good warm-up before Ocean Course.

top_courses.name: Turtle Point
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design. 3 holes along the Atlantic. Recently renovated.

top_courses.name: Cougar Point
top_courses.must_know: Gary Player design along the Kiawah River. Shortest and most accessible course on the island.

hidden_gems.name: Charleston Municipal Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: In Charleston proper. Basic but playable. Seth Raynor design from 1925. Great if you add a Charleston day.

hidden_gems.name: Links at Stono Ferry
hidden_gems.must_know: 20 min from Kiawah. Good value course on the Stono River marsh. Quiet and scenic.

lodging_options.name: The Sanctuary at Kiawah Island
lodging_options.note: 5-star luxury. Ocean Course access. The ultimate Kiawah experience.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah Island Golf Resort (villas)
lodging_options.note: Villas and cottages across the island. Best option for groups. Pool, beach, bikes included.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah rental home
lodging_options.note: Inside the gate. Need resort access to play Ocean Course.

dining.name: The Ocean Room
dining.group_note: At The Sanctuary. Ocean views. Black tie optional. Celebration dinner.

dining.name: Tomasso at Turtle Point
dining.group_note: Best casual upscale on island. Great pasta.

dining.name: Husk (Charleston)
dining.group_note: 45 min away in Charleston. James Beard winner. Iconic Southern cuisine.

dining.name: FIG (Charleston)
dining.group_note: Charleston's best restaurant per many. Reserve 3+ weeks out.

insider_tips: Play Ocean Course on a calm day if possible — wind can make it unplayable for high handicappers
Pair Kiawah with a Charleston day for the food — Husk, FIG, and Rodney Scott's BBQ are worth the drive
Stay in a villa, not The Sanctuary, unless it's a special occasion. Villas are more fun for groups
Osprey Point on arrival day, Ocean Course day 2 when you're warmed up and rested
Caddie on Ocean Course is worth every penny — they know the wind and the greens
Spring (Apr-May) is the sweet spot — warm, flowers blooming, before summer humidity hits
destinations.kit_tagline: Play the Ocean Course, survive the wind, eat your way through Charleston's James Beard scene.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-April hits peak spring conditions before humidity climbs and after azaleas bloom.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival day round after CHS landing — Osprey is forgiving enough to shake off travel rust.
Early tee when you're rested and wind is calmest — Ocean Course demands your best energy and focus.
Morning round before Charleston drive — Nicklaus layout with 3 ocean holes is a solid closer without the Ocean Course grind.
Checkout and drive to CHS — no golf scheduled unless you have a late flight and want to add Cougar Point.

recommended_lodging.name: Kiawah Island Golf Resort (villas)
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Villas give you space to spread out, full kitchen for breakfast savings, and proximity to all courses. More fun for groups than hotel rooms at The Sanctuary unless someone's celebrating an anniversary.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 4-5 months out for spring dates

bonus_plays.name: Husk
bonus_plays.why: 45-minute drive to Charleston on Day 3 evening after Turtle Point. James Beard-winning Southern cooking — shrimp and grits, cornbread, whatever's in season. Worth the drive every time.

bonus_plays.name: The Ocean Room
bonus_plays.why: Black-tie-optional celebration dinner at The Sanctuary after you've survived the Ocean Course. Ocean views, prime ribeye, full wine list. Book ahead.

bonus_plays.name: Beach cart / bike rental
bonus_plays.why: 30+ miles of paved trails across the island. Rent bikes or a beach cart on Day 2 afternoon post-Ocean Course to decompress before dinner.

bonus_plays.name: Ryder Cup Bar at The Sanctuary
bonus_plays.why: Whiskey library and cigar terrace overlooking the Ocean Course. Post-round ritual spot even if you're not staying there.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 15 min from OTH, 3 hrs from EUG
destinations.avoid_reason: Heavy rain and wind. Not worth the premium in winter.
destinations.why_go: The greatest golf resort in America. Five world-class courses, all walking only, on the rugged Oregon coast. No houses, no roads, no distractions — just golf. Mecca for the serious golfer.

top_courses.name: Pacific Dunes
top_courses.must_know: #1 resort course in America. Tom Doak masterpiece. 11 holes with ocean views.

top_courses.name: Bandon Dunes
top_courses.must_know: The original. Ocean cliff holes on back 9 are jaw-dropping. The course that started it all.

top_courses.name: Sheep Ranch
top_courses.must_know: Newest course (2020). Every hole has ocean views. Wide open, few bunkers. Most 'links' of all five.

top_courses.name: Old Macdonald
top_courses.must_know: Tribute to golden-age architecture. Massive double greens, huge fairways. Most unique of the five.

top_courses.name: Bandon Trails
top_courses.must_know: Inland routing through coastal forest. No ocean but stunning. Feels like a different world.

hidden_gems.name: Bandon Preserve
hidden_gems.must_know: On-site par-3 with ocean views. All proceeds to charity. Perfect arrival day.

hidden_gems.name: The Punchbowl
hidden_gems.must_know: Massive putting green by Tom Doak. Free for guests. Bet on it.

lodging_options.name: Bandon Dunes Resort (Lodge/Cottages)
lodging_options.note: On-site. Walk to all courses. Lodge rooms simple but comfortable. Communal vibe.

dining.name: The Gallery
dining.group_note: Best meal on property. Pacific NW cuisine.

dining.name: McKee's Pub
dining.group_note: THE post-round hub. Good whiskey selection.

dining.name: Trails End Cookhouse
dining.group_note: Outdoor fire pits. Great for big groups.

insider_tips: Book 12+ months out for peak season (Jun-Sep)
Pacific Dunes + Bandon Dunes are the top 2 — schedule mid-trip when playing well
Forecaddies for groups — one caddie per foursome, you carry/push bags
Bring layers — 65° and sunny at 8am, 50° with rain by noon
Fly into OTH if possible — 15 min vs 3+ hrs from Eugene
NOT a nightlife trip. Golf monastery. Early rounds, pub dinner, bed by 10.
destinations.kit_tagline: Five Tom Doak and Coore/Crenshaw courses on cliff edges where links golf was meant to be played.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-September offers stable weather after summer crowds thin and before October wind picks up.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival day par-3 lets group shake off travel and dial in short game before the real test starts.
Ease into trip with widest fairways and most forgiving design before tackling the harder tracks.
Play the #1 course mid-trip when swings are grooved and before wind gets nasty.
Back nine cliff holes deserve good legs and clear heads — morning start before fatigue sets in.
Send-off round on the widest, most scenic layout — early start allows noon checkout and afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Bandon Dunes Resort (Lodge/Cottages)
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: On-site is the only move. Walking to tee times, pub crawl to McKee's, no designated driver. The communal vibe in the Lodge is half the trip.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 12 months out for Jun-Sep dates

bonus_plays.name: The Punchbowl
bonus_plays.why: Free Tom Doak putting course. Run a team match the first evening while sun sets. Sets the tone.

bonus_plays.name: Trails End Cookhouse
bonus_plays.why: Outdoor fire pits and BBQ work for groups. Order family-style and settle into the pace of the place.

bonus_plays.name: McKee's Pub
bonus_plays.why: The post-round ritual. Whiskey selection is legitimate and every group ends up here anyway.

destinations.avoid_reason: Extreme humidity and heat. Bugs relentless.
destinations.why_go: Historic charm, incredible food scene, solid resort golf. Downtown is walkable and dripping with Southern character. The golf isn't Hilton Head-level but the total trip experience is elite.

top_courses.name: The Club at Savannah Harbor
top_courses.must_know: Resort course on Hutchinson Island. Water taxi to River Street. Best option near downtown.

top_courses.name: Crosswinds Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Best public option. No frills but well-maintained.

top_courses.name: Savannah Quarters (Nicklaus)
top_courses.must_know: Nicklaus design in Pooler. Good value. 20 min from downtown.

hidden_gems.name: Palmetto Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Oldest course in Georgia (1892). Historic and charming.

lodging_options.name: Westin Savannah Harbor
lodging_options.note: On-site course. Water taxi to River Street.

lodging_options.name: Historic district townhouse
lodging_options.note: Restored townhouses. Walk to bars/restaurants.

dining.name: The Grey
dining.group_note: Mashama Bailey's James Beard winner. Best meal in Savannah.

dining.name: Mrs. Wilkes' Dining Room
dining.group_note: Communal Southern lunch. Line at 10:30am. Cash only. Once in a lifetime.

dining.name: Husk Savannah
dining.group_note: Sean Brock's outpost. Outstanding.

dining.name: Treylor Park
dining.group_note: PB&J wings. Great cocktails. Late night.

insider_tips: Savannah is a food + drinking + history trip with golf — lean into that
Open container laws — get a to-go cup from any bar
Play golf mornings, explore downtown afternoons, big dinner nights
Tybee Island 20 min east for beach day
April during azalea season is most beautiful
destinations.kit_tagline: Historic charm and James Beard dining with golf between meals — Savannah is a food trip first.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-April hits azalea season peak, comfortable temps before summer humidity sets in.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most flights land late morning. Use afternoon for check-in and downtown exploration instead of forcing a round.
Morning round at the best track near downtown before humidity peaks. Water taxi back to River Street for lunch.
Early morning Nicklaus design in Pooler. Finish by noon, save afternoon for Tybee Island beach or Forsyth Park.
Final round at the no-frills public track. Early tee gives time for checkout and travel without rushing.

recommended_lodging.name: Historic district townhouse
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Walking distance to every bar and restaurant worth hitting. For 6-8 guys, splitting a townhouse beats resort pricing and puts you in the middle of the action.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 4-5 months out. April azalea season books early.

bonus_plays.name: Mrs. Wilkes' Dining Room
bonus_plays.why: Communal Southern lunch. Line forms at 10:30am. Cash only. Fried chicken and sides passed family-style. Once in a lifetime meal.

bonus_plays.name: The Grey
bonus_plays.why: Mashama Bailey's James Beard winner in a converted Greyhound bus terminal. Best meal in Savannah. Book the night you confirm the trip.

bonus_plays.name: River Street bar crawl with to-go cups
bonus_plays.why: Open container laws mean you walk bar to bar with drinks in hand. Get a to-go cup from any bar and lean into it.

bonus_plays.name: Tybee Island beach day
bonus_plays.why: 20 minutes east. Use Day 3 afternoon after morning golf to get out of downtown and hit the coast.

destinations.avoid_reason: Hurricane season. Courses may close.
destinations.why_go: Desert-meets-ocean courses unlike anything in the US. Nicklaus and Dye designs with Sea of Cortez views. All-inclusive resorts, fishing, Cabo nightlife.

top_courses.name: Quivira Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Crown jewel. Holes cut into granite cliffs above Pacific. Must stay at Pueblo Bonito/Quivira resort.

top_courses.name: Cabo del Sol (Ocean Course)
top_courses.must_know: Nicklaus: 'best piece of golf property I've ever seen.' 7 holes on Sea of Cortez.

top_courses.name: Diamante (Dunes Course)
top_courses.must_know: Davis Love III links on Pacific dunes. Walking encouraged. Bandon Dunes in Mexico.

top_courses.name: Palmilla Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Nicklaus 27-hole. More forgiving. Good value for area.

hidden_gems.name: Club Campestre San José
hidden_gems.must_know: Nicklaus design. Less crowded, cheaper than marquee courses.

lodging_options.name: Pueblo Bonito Sunset Beach
lodging_options.note: Quivira access. All-inclusive saves on food/drink.

lodging_options.name: Cabo corridor villa
lodging_options.note: Pool, ocean view, chef service available.

dining.name: Edith's
dining.group_note: Open-air, live music, great steaks/lobster. Institution.

dining.name: Manta (Cape Hotel)
dining.group_note: Enrique Olvera. World-class.

dining.name: Tacos Gardenias
dining.group_note: Best fish tacos in Cabo. Cash only.

dining.name: El Squid Roe
dining.group_note: Legendary Cabo party bar. One night mandatory.

insider_tips: All-inclusive resort saves massive money on food/drinks
Quivira is the must-play — one of the most spectacular on Earth
Passport required. Check everyone's.
Use Uber — taxis overcharge tourists
Fishing is incredible — half-day charter mandatory for non-golf time
Don't drink tap water
Nov-Dec is prime: peak weather, fewer crowds, slightly lower prices
destinations.kit_tagline: Nicklaus cliffside golf above the Pacific, all-inclusive eating, and marlin fishing between rounds.

default_recommended_dates.reason: November hits peak weather, fewer crowds than winter, and slightly lower rates than December-February.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most SJD flights land afternoon. Use day for settling in, range session, and welcome dinner at resort.
Early start for crown jewel course. Full energy needed for cliffside holes and difficult layout.
Morning round before heat. Afternoon open for fishing charter or beach recovery.
Links course walkable in morning temps. Pacific breeze manageable early, picks up afternoon.
Early departure round. More forgiving Nicklaus layout, back to resort by noon for checkout and SJD transfer.

recommended_lodging.name: Pueblo Bonito Sunset Beach
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: All-inclusive saves $50-75/person/day on food and drinks, which matters at Cabo prices. Quivira access is automatic for guests. Pool area handles groups well.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 4-5 months out for November dates, rooms fill fast in peak season.

bonus_plays.name: Edith's
bonus_plays.why: Open-air institution with live music. Groups fit easily, steaks and lobster are the move, atmosphere is classic Cabo without being a scene.

bonus_plays.name: El Squid Roe
bonus_plays.why: Legendary Cabo party bar. One night mandatory. Go Day 3 after the fishing charter.

bonus_plays.name: Half-day fishing charter
bonus_plays.why: Marlin capital of the world. Incredible fishing and non-golf activity that matters. Book afternoon Day 3 after morning round.

bonus_plays.name: Tacos Gardenias
bonus_plays.why: Best fish tacos in Cabo. Cash only. Cheap, fast, perfect for last-night casual dinner before flights.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 10 min from BKG, 45 min from SGF
destinations.avoid_reason: Cold and most attractions/courses closed or limited.
destinations.why_go: Best bang-for-your-buck golf trip in the Midwest. Ozark mountain scenery, courses under $100, lakeside lodging, and just enough nightlife to keep it fun. Perfect for dads trips and big reunion groups.

top_courses.name: Top of the Rock (Par-3 Course)
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus par-3 course at Big Cedar Lodge. Caves, waterfalls, Table Rock Lake views. Hosted the Bass Pro Legends of Golf. Not a real round but an experience.

top_courses.name: Payne's Valley (Tiger Woods Design)
top_courses.must_know: Tiger Woods' first public course design. 19th hole is a par-3 island green. At Big Cedar Lodge. The showpiece of Branson golf.

top_courses.name: Ozarks National
top_courses.must_know: Coore & Crenshaw design at Big Cedar. Links-style in the Ozarks — ridgeline routing with 360° views. Walking encouraged.

top_courses.name: Branson Hills Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Chuck Smith design. Best value course in Branson. Ozark terrain, good conditions, won't break the bank.

hidden_gems.name: Ledgestone Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Semi-private but public access available. Tom Clark design. Beautiful Ozark routing.

hidden_gems.name: Holiday Hills Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Basic but fun. Short course, cheap rate, good for a casual round when the group needs a breather.

lodging_options.name: Big Cedar Lodge
lodging_options.note: Bass Pro's flagship resort. Cabins on Table Rock Lake. On-site courses. THE Branson golf resort.

lodging_options.name: Table Rock Lake cabin rental
lodging_options.note: Lakefront cabins. Fire pit, dock, grills. Perfect for big groups.

lodging_options.name: Branson strip hotels
lodging_options.note: Budget hotels along 76 Country Blvd. Nothing fancy but cheap and functional.

dining.name: Top of the Rock (Osage Restaurant)
dining.group_note: At Big Cedar. Stunning views. Best upscale meal in Branson.

dining.name: Gettin' Basted BBQ
dining.group_note: Award-winning BBQ. The pulled pork is incredible. Casual, big portions.

dining.name: Florentina's Ristorante
dining.group_note: Best Italian in Branson. Good for a nicer dinner without Big Cedar prices.

dining.name: Billy Gail's Cafe
dining.group_note: Famous for hubcap-sized pancakes. Cash only. The pre-round fuel stop.

non_golf_activities: Top of the Rock cave tour
Go-karts at Track Family Fun Parks
insider_tips: Big Cedar Lodge is the anchor — Payne's Valley + Ozarks National + Top of the Rock are all there
Book Big Cedar 3+ months out — it sells out, especially in fall
Branson Hills is the budget add-on round — $40-80 for solid Ozark golf
Table Rock Lake pontoon rental for a non-golf day — bring a cooler, bring music
Fall (Oct) has the best foliage in the Ozarks — stunning colors on every hole
Drive from SGF airport — Branson's airport has limited flights and higher fares
destinations.kit_tagline: Tiger Woods design, Coore & Crenshaw links, and a Jack par-3 over waterfalls — all under a grand per guy.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-October hits peak Ozark foliage — every hole has color, and Big Cedar availability is still decent before late-month sellout.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival day with SGF landing around 11am — par-3 is the perfect settle-in round without burning the group on travel fatigue.
Early start for Tiger's showpiece while energy is high — play the 19th island hole before afternoon crowds and heat.
Coore & Crenshaw links routing works best in morning calm — ridgeline exposure means wind picks up by noon in October.
Budget finisher on departure day — early tee gives 3+ hours to airport after the round, and $50 rate doesn't sting on checkout morning.

recommended_lodging.name: Big Cedar Lodge
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Three of your four rounds are on-site — zero drive time to Payne's Valley, Ozarks National, and Top of the Rock. You're paying for convenience and the full Big Cedar experience, not just a bed.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 3+ months out — sells out in fall, especially October foliage weeks.

bonus_plays.name: Osage Restaurant at Top of the Rock
bonus_plays.why: Best upscale meal in Branson with Table Rock Lake views — do this Day 2 night after Payne's Valley when the group is riding high.

bonus_plays.name: Table Rock Lake pontoon rental
bonus_plays.why: Day 3 afternoon after Ozarks National — cooler, music, and a few hours on the water before the final round. Splits 8 ways for $40/guy.

bonus_plays.name: Gettin' Basted BBQ
bonus_plays.why: Award-winning pulled pork, big portions, casual vibe — perfect Day 1 welcome dinner after Top of the Rock par-3 round.

bonus_plays.name: Lost Canyon Cave Tour
bonus_plays.why: 30-minute walk through Ozark caves at Big Cedar — good leg-stretcher on arrival day before dinner, and it's right there.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 45-60 min from PNS, 60-75 min from MOB
destinations.avoid_reason: Peak heat/humidity, hurricane risk, and peak tourist season.
destinations.why_go: The Robert Trent Jones Trail's Gulf Coast stops are criminally underrated — world-class architecture at muni prices. Add white sand beaches, seafood, and incredibly affordable lodging. The best-kept secret in budget golf trips.

top_courses.name: Kiva Dunes Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Links-style on the Gulf of Mexico. Jerry Pate design. Wind is always a factor. Best course on the Alabama coast.

top_courses.name: Craft Farms (Cotton Creek)
top_courses.must_know: Arnold Palmer design. Two courses on the property — Cotton Creek is the better one. Good value, forgiving for all skill levels.

top_courses.name: Peninsula Golf & Racquet Club
top_courses.must_know: Rees Jones design on Mobile Bay. Marsh and bay views. 27 holes — play the Lakes and Marsh nines for the best combo.

top_courses.name: RTJ Trail — Magnolia Grove (Crossings)
top_courses.must_know: Part of the Robert Trent Jones Golf Trail. 45 min north in Mobile. 54 holes, Crossings is the flagship. Insane value for RTJ design quality.

hidden_gems.name: Lakewood Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: At the Lakewood resort in Point Clear. 36 holes on Mobile Bay. Charming, old-school Southern resort feel.

hidden_gems.name: TimberCreek Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: In Daphne, 30 min north. Solid muni-level course with good conditions. Cheapest playable round in the area.

lodging_options.name: Gulf Shores beachfront condo
lodging_options.note: Right on the beach. Kitchen saves on meals. VRBO has tons of options.

lodging_options.name: The Lodge at Gulf State Park (Hilton)
lodging_options.note: Beach resort with pool. No golf on-site but central to everything.

lodging_options.name: Orange Beach rental house
lodging_options.note: More space than condos. Pool houses available. Good for 8+ groups.

dining.name: The Hangout
dining.group_note: On the beach. Live music, sand volleyball, communal tables. THE Gulf Shores hangout.

dining.name: Fisher's at Orange Beach Marina
dining.group_note: Fresh off the boat. Dockside dining. Best seafood in the area.

dining.name: Lulu's (Jimmy Buffett's sister)
dining.group_note: On the ICW. Fun atmosphere, big groups welcome. Cheeseburger in Paradise vibes.

dining.name: GT's on the Bay
dining.group_note: Upscale option on Wolf Bay. Good for the nice dinner night.

insider_tips: Kiva Dunes is the marquee round — play it on the calmest wind day for the best experience
RTJ Trail at Magnolia Grove is 45 min north but the value is unbeatable — 36 holes for under $100
Beachfront condos with kitchens are the move — cook breakfast, eat seafood out for dinner
Flora-Bama is the legendary bar on the FL/AL state line — one night there is mandatory
Fall (Sep-Oct) is the sweet spot: warm water, cheap lodging, no crowds, shoulder-season golf rates
Fly into Pensacola for more flight options — it's worth the extra 20 min drive

items.title: Arrive PNS, drive to Gulf Shores condo

destinations.kit_tagline: RTJ Trail courses at muni prices, white sand beaches, and Flora-Bama — the budget trip that doesn't feel like one.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-October hits the fall sweet spot: shoulder-season golf rates, warm Gulf water, and no summer crowds.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most flights into PNS arrive late morning — use afternoon for beach and settling into the condo.
Early start catches the calmest wind on the links — Gulf breeze picks up by noon and changes the entire course.
Palmer design is more forgiving than Kiva — good recovery round after yesterday's wind test.
Early round on the bay, done by noon — leaves time for checkout and the drive to PNS for afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Gulf Shores beachfront condo
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Kitchen saves $15-20 per guy per day on breakfasts and post-round meals. Right on the beach for the mandatory afternoon sessions. VRBO has dozens of options with this exact setup.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 3-4 months out for fall dates, 4-5 months for spring.

bonus_plays.name: Flora-Bama
bonus_plays.why: The legendary honky tonk on the Alabama-Florida state line. One night here is mandatory — live music, mullet toss contests, and the most Gulf Shores experience you can have.

bonus_plays.name: Fisher's at Orange Beach Marina
bonus_plays.why: Fresh off the boat at the docks. Best seafood in the area and the right spot for the big group dinner night.

bonus_plays.name: RTJ Trail — Magnolia Grove
bonus_plays.why: If the group wants one more round, the 45-minute drive north to Mobile gets you 36 holes of RTJ Trail for under $100. Insane value.

bonus_plays.name: Jet ski rentals
bonus_plays.why: Gulf waters are warm in fall. Two-hour rental splits across the group and fills the afternoon gap between rounds.

destinations.avoid_reason: Courses closed for winter/snow. Tahoe is a ski destination Oct-Apr.
destinations.why_go: Mountain golf at 6,200+ feet elevation — your drives go 10-15% farther. Crystal-clear lake, pine forests, and casino nightlife on the Nevada side. Perfect summer escape.

top_courses.name: Edgewood Tahoe Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Hosts the American Century Celebrity Championship. Holes along Lake Tahoe are world-class views. George Fazio design. THE must-play at Tahoe.

top_courses.name: Old Greenwood
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design in Truckee. Mountain meadow setting. Wider fairways, good for all skill levels. 15 min from North Shore.

top_courses.name: Coyote Moon Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Carved through pine forest in Truckee. Some of the most dramatic elevation changes in golf. Brad Bell design. Hidden gem.

top_courses.name: Incline Village Championship Course
top_courses.must_know: Robert Trent Jones Sr. design on the North Shore. Lake views, tight mountain layout. Challenging but beautiful.

hidden_gems.name: Tahoe Donner Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: In Truckee. Shorter mountain course. Great conditions, deer on the fairways. Best value at Tahoe.

hidden_gems.name: The Golf Courses at Incline Village (Mountain)
hidden_gems.must_know: Executive 18-hole course. Par-58. Fun, fast, and cheap. Good arrival day activity.

lodging_options.name: Edgewood Tahoe Resort
lodging_options.note: Luxury lakefront. On-site course. The splurge option.

lodging_options.name: Harrah's / Harvey's (South Shore)
lodging_options.note: Casino hotels with everything. Pool, restaurants, gaming. Stateline NV location.

lodging_options.name: Tahoe cabin rental
lodging_options.note: Best for groups. Hot tub, mountain views, fire pit. Book on VRBO/Airbnb.

dining.name: Edgewood Restaurant
dining.group_note: At the resort. Lake views. Celebration dinner.

dining.name: Gar Woods Grill
dining.group_note: North Shore lakefront. Great deck. Famous Wet Woody cocktail.

dining.name: Moody's Bistro (Truckee)
dining.group_note: Downtown Truckee. Live jazz, great food. Best restaurant in the area.

dining.name: Base Camp Pizza
dining.group_note: South Lake Tahoe. Wood-fired pizza, craft beer. Perfect casual night.

insider_tips: Your ball flies 10-15% farther at altitude — club down and enjoy the bombs
Edgewood is the bucket list round — book 30+ days out for peak summer
Stay on South Shore for casino nightlife, North Shore for quieter mountain vibe
Truckee (15 min from North Shore) has the best restaurant scene at Tahoe
July-August is peak — book lodging and tee times 2-3 months out
Mountain weather changes fast — bring layers even in July. Morning rounds can be 50°F

items.title: Arrive RNO, drive to Tahoe cabin

destinations.kit_tagline: Mountain golf at 6,200 feet where your drives bomb 10-15% farther and the lake makes every round a postcard.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-June avoids peak July-August pricing and crowds while weather is fully dialed in — courses are open, temps are 70s, and tee times book easier.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Afternoon tee after RNO arrival and cabin check-in — gives you time to settle and lets you experience the dramatic elevation changes when shadows make them even more striking.
Early morning before wind picks up on the lake — holes 16 and 17 play best in calm conditions and you want every second of those lakeside views.
Morning round on the Nicklaus track after Edgewood — wider fairways and forgiving layout give your group a breather before departure day.
Checkout and RNO departure — no golf, 45-minute drive to airport with buffer.

recommended_lodging.name: Tahoe cabin rental
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Four-bedroom cabin splits to under $120/night per person for 8 guys and gives you the hot tub, fire pit, and kitchen to save $15-20/person/day on breakfasts. Better bathroom ratio than a resort and you're not walking through a casino at midnight.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 2-3 months out for peak summer dates

bonus_plays.name: Moody's Bistro
bonus_plays.why: Best restaurant in the Tahoe area — live jazz, downtown Truckee vibe, and you're 10 minutes from your cabin. Book a table for 8 after Coyote Moon.

bonus_plays.name: Gar Woods Grill deck
bonus_plays.why: North Shore lakefront deck with the famous Wet Woody cocktail — post-Edgewood celebration spot before you head to the cabin or South Shore casinos.

bonus_plays.name: Casino night at Harrah's
bonus_plays.why: South Shore is 30 minutes from North Shore but worth the drive for one night — blackjack, craps, and the full Nevada experience. Set a loss limit.

bonus_plays.name: Incline Village Mountain Course
bonus_plays.why: Par-58 executive track for $50 if you want to squeeze in 9 on arrival day before Coyote Moon or as a Day 3 afternoon add-on. Fast and fun.

destinations.avoid_reason: 110°F+ desert heat. Courses offer dirt-cheap summer rates but it's brutal.
destinations.why_go: Desert golf at half the price of Vegas or Scottsdale. Wolf Creek alone is worth the trip — one of the most visually spectacular courses on Earth. Add 5-6 other solid courses, casino hotels under $100/night, and you have an incredible budget trip.

top_courses.name: Wolf Creek Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Most visually dramatic course in America. 200ft elevation drops from tee to fairway. Canyon walls, desert colors. Bring extra balls and a camera.

top_courses.name: CasaBlanca Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: At the CasaBlanca resort. Good desert course, well-maintained. Best value for staying + playing in Mesquite.

top_courses.name: Conestoga Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Gary Panks design with red rock canyon views. Good mix of challenge and playability.

top_courses.name: Falcon Ridge Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Budget-friendly option. Solid layout through desert terrain. Good for the budget round.

hidden_gems.name: Coyote Springs Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: 30 min south toward Vegas. Nicklaus design. Massive development that never materialized — world-class course at a fraction of what it should cost.

hidden_gems.name: Sand Hollow Resort (Utah)
hidden_gems.must_know: 45 min north in St. George, UT. Red rock desert golf. Championship course is stunning.

lodging_options.name: CasaBlanca Resort
lodging_options.note: On-site course, casino, pool, restaurants. Best all-in-one option.

lodging_options.name: Eureka Casino Resort
lodging_options.note: Budget casino hotel. Clean rooms, good buffet. No-frills base camp.

lodging_options.name: Mesquite rental house
lodging_options.note: Golf community houses with mountain views. Good for big groups.

dining.name: Katherine's Steakhouse (CasaBlanca)
dining.group_note: Best restaurant in Mesquite. At the resort. Good steaks, reasonable prices.

dining.name: Peggy Sue's Diner
dining.group_note: On I-15 in Yermo. Classic roadside diner. Fun pit stop on the drive from Vegas.

dining.name: Skydome Lounge (CasaBlanca)
dining.group_note: Sports bar with pool tables. Where the group ends up every night.

dining.name: George's Corner
dining.group_note: In St. George if you venture to Sand Hollow. Great burgers and shakes.

non_golf_activities: Valley of Fire State Park (30 min)
Zion National Park day trip (90 min)
insider_tips: Wolf Creek is the ENTIRE reason to come here — plan everything around it
Stay at CasaBlanca for convenience — course + casino + hotel + restaurants in one spot
Drive from Las Vegas is scenic (I-15 through Valley of Fire area). Not a bad drive at all.
Play Wolf Creek morning, CasaBlanca afternoon for the perfect contrast day
If you extend to 4 days, do a Zion National Park day trip — it's 90 min and life-changing
Mesquite in November is perfect: 70°F days, low rates, uncrowded courses

items.title: Arrive LAS, drive to Mesquite (80 min)
Drive to LAS, depart (stop at Valley of Fire optional)

destinations.kit_tagline: Desert golf for half what Vegas charges, anchored by the most dramatic course in America.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-November hits the sweet spot: 70°F days, low rates, and courses are empty.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival round after the 80-min drive from LAS. CasaBlanca lets you ease in before Wolf Creek tomorrow.
Early start for the headliner. Morning light on the canyon walls is unbeatable, and you want fresh legs for this walk.
Gary Panks design with red rock views. Good challenge without the Wolf Creek exhaustion factor.
Budget-friendly final round. Early tee gets you back to LAS with plenty of buffer for afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: CasaBlanca Resort
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: On-site course, casino, pool, and Katherine's Steakhouse all in one spot. You'll walk out of your room and onto the first tee. After Wolf Creek, the group will collapse at Skydome Lounge without needing a car.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 3-4 months out for November rates under $90/night.

bonus_plays.name: Katherine's Steakhouse
bonus_plays.why: Best restaurant in Mesquite. Book a table for Day 2 after Wolf Creek — the group will want a proper meal and some war stories.

bonus_plays.name: Skydome Lounge
bonus_plays.why: Sports bar with pool tables at CasaBlanca. This is where you end up every night whether you plan it or not.

bonus_plays.name: Valley of Fire State Park
bonus_plays.why: 30 minutes on the drive back to Vegas. Pull over for 45 minutes of red rock formations and photo ops. Beats sitting in the airport.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 60 min from MSN, 2.5 hrs from MKE
destinations.avoid_reason: Courses closed for winter. Wisconsin winters are brutal.
destinations.why_go: Sand Valley is the Bandon Dunes of the Midwest — world-ranked courses, walking only, no pretension. Built on ancient sand deposits that create links-like terrain in central Wisconsin. The golf cognoscenti know about this place.

top_courses.name: Sand Valley
top_courses.must_know: Coore & Crenshaw design on sand dunes in the Wisconsin Northwoods. Wide fairways, strategic bunkering, walking only. The original course that put this place on the map.

top_courses.name: Mammoth Dunes
top_courses.must_know: David McLay Kidd design. Widest fairways in golf — some 80+ yards. Incredibly fun and forgiving while still strategic. Many prefer it to Sand Valley.

top_courses.name: The Lido
top_courses.must_know: Painstaking recreation of the legendary 1917 C.B. Macdonald course that was destroyed in WWII. Opened 2023. One of the most anticipated courses in decades.

top_courses.name: Sedge Valley (par-3)
top_courses.must_know: On-site par-3 course. Fun, fast, and a great way to settle bets on the last day.

hidden_gems.name: Lawsonia Links
hidden_gems.must_know: 30 min south in Green Lake. Langford & Moreau design from 1930. Top 100 value course in America. Essential add-on.

hidden_gems.name: Wild Rock Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: At the Wilderness Resort in the Dells. Good family-friendly option with waterpark on-site.

lodging_options.name: Sand Valley Resort (cottages/lodge)
lodging_options.note: On-site. Cottages for groups, lodge rooms for smaller parties. Fire pits, communal dining. The only option for the full experience.

lodging_options.name: Wisconsin Dells hotels
lodging_options.note: Waterpark hotels galore. Budget option, 30 min from Sand Valley. More for families.

dining.name: Craig's Porch
dining.group_note: At Sand Valley Resort. Great food, overlooking the course. The gathering spot.

dining.name: Mammoth Bar
dining.group_note: Post-round beers, casual food. Fire pit outside.

dining.name: Ishnala Supper Club
dining.group_note: Wisconsin tradition. On Mirror Lake, 30 min away. Old-fashioned cocktails, prime rib. A must.

dining.name: Field's at the Wilderness
dining.group_note: In the Dells. Good steakhouse option if staying off-site.

insider_tips: Sand Valley is the Midwest's Bandon — treat it the same way. Golf monastery, not nightlife trip.
Play all three 18-hole courses if you have 3+ days. The Lido is the newest and most talked-about.
Mammoth Dunes is the most fun if you have higher handicappers — 80-yard-wide fairways are forgiving
Lawsonia Links is 30 min south and a TOP value add — $50-100 for a top-100-caliber course
Book 3+ months out for peak summer. Sand Valley has limited capacity and sells out.
Wisconsin supper clubs are a cultural experience — go to Ishnala for the old-fashioned + prime rib ritual
Fly into Madison for the best flight options. The 60-min drive through farm country is scenic.

items.title: Arrive MSN, drive to Sand Valley (60 min)

destinations.kit_tagline: Ancient sand dunes in central Wisconsin that play like Scottish links, minus the ocean and the pretension.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-June hits peak conditions after spring rain but before high summer sellouts and heat.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival day with Madison morning flights. Mammoth's width is forgiving when your swing is rusty from travel.
The original. Morning tee before wind picks up and to leave afternoon open for a second round if the group is feeling strong.
The hardest of the three. Play it when you're warmed up but not exhausted. 36-hole day for the full monastery experience.
30-minute drive south to Green Lake. Top-100 value course at a third of the price. Early tee leaves afternoon for Sedge Valley.
Par-3 track on-site. Fast, fun, and the perfect way to settle last-day bets without a full 18.
Checkout and 60-minute drive to Madison. No golf unless you have a late afternoon flight.

recommended_lodging.name: Sand Valley Resort (cottages/lodge)
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: On-site is the only way to do this right. Cottages sleep 4-8 with common areas for cards and whiskey. Fire pits, walking distance to courses, communal dining at Craig's Porch. The golf monastery experience requires staying at the monastery.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 3+ months out for summer dates. Limited capacity means peak weekends sell out early.

bonus_plays.name: Ishnala Supper Club
bonus_plays.why: Wisconsin supper club on Mirror Lake, 30 minutes away. Old-fashioned cocktails and prime rib ritual are non-negotiable cultural experience. Reserve ahead.

bonus_plays.name: Mammoth Bar
bonus_plays.why: Post-round spot on-site. Fire pit outside, casual food, and the place to replay shots with the group. Open late.

bonus_plays.name: Fire pit + putting contest at resort
bonus_plays.why: Use the practice greens for a side-game contest. Loser buys the whiskey round. Wisconsin nights are perfect for this.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 90 min from EDI, 2 hrs from GLA
destinations.avoid_reason: Cold, wet, short daylight hours. Some courses close or have limited availability.
destinations.why_go: The Home of Golf. The Old Course is where it all started. Walking the same fairways as Bobby Jones, Jack Nicklaus, and Tiger Woods is a spiritual experience for any golfer. Plus Scotland's whisky, pubs, and countryside are world-class.

top_courses.name: The Old Course at St Andrews
top_courses.must_know: Ballot system — apply 2 days before, results at 4pm. Or book a guaranteed tee time through Old Course Experience package (£££). Walking only, caddie essential. Sunday is closed (rest day tradition). The Swilcan Bridge on #18 is the most famous photo in golf.
top_courses.booking_lead_time: Ballot 2 days prior, or book package 12+ months out

top_courses.name: The New Course (St Andrews Links)
top_courses.must_know: Don't let the name fool you — it opened in 1895. Excellent links golf without the Old Course lottery. Often available same-day.

top_courses.name: Kingsbarns Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: 15 min from St Andrews. Clifftop links with North Sea views on nearly every hole. Many say it's the best 'modern links' course in Scotland.

top_courses.name: Carnoustie Golf Links (Championship)
top_courses.must_know: 30 min from St Andrews. 'Car-nasty' is the hardest Open Championship venue. Barry Burn on #18 has decided Opens. For low handicappers.

hidden_gems.name: Crail Golfing Society (Balcomie Links)
hidden_gems.must_know: 7th oldest club in the world. Clifftop links in a tiny fishing village 10 min from St Andrews. Authentic, uncrowded, stunning.

hidden_gems.name: Elie Golf House Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Uses a periscope in the starter's hut to check the 1st fairway. Charming links course overlooking the Firth of Forth. Pure Scottish golf.

lodging_options.name: Old Course Hotel
lodging_options.note: Overlooks the Road Hole (#17). Iconic. Kohler spa. Book 6+ months out.

lodging_options.name: Rusacks St Andrews
lodging_options.note: On the 18th hole of the Old Course. Recently renovated. Rooftop bar.

lodging_options.name: St Andrews B&Bs/guesthouses
lodging_options.note: Plenty of B&Bs in town. Walking distance to everything. Book early for summer.

lodging_options.name: St Andrews flat/cottage
lodging_options.note: Town is walkable. Get something on The Scores for ocean views.

dining.name: The Jigger Inn
dining.group_note: Adjacent to the Old Course Hotel. Historic pub. THE post-round pint spot.

dining.name: Forgans
dining.group_note: On Market Street. Great cocktails, solid food. Upstairs bar is lively.

dining.name: Adamson
dining.group_note: Best restaurant in St Andrews. Reserve ahead. Worth one splurge night.

dining.name: Tailend Fish Bar
dining.group_note: Best fish & chips in town. Takeaway or sit down. Essential.

dining.name: Vic's Bar
dining.group_note: Traditional Scottish pub. Good whisky selection. Locals' favorite.

non_golf_activities: Walk along West Sands beach (Chariots of Fire)
insider_tips: Enter the Old Course ballot early — results come at 4pm, 2 days before. Have a backup plan.
If you miss the ballot, show up as a single at dawn for a walk-on — it works more than you'd think
A caddie on the Old Course is non-negotiable. They know every hidden bunker and slope.
Play Kingsbarns the day before the Old Course — it's spectacular and gets you links-ready
Bring rain gear and layers for EVERY round. Scottish weather changes every 30 minutes.
Pint at the Jigger Inn after the Old Course is a sacred ritual. Don't skip it.
Passport required. Check visa requirements. No issues for US citizens for short stays.
Rent a car — courses are spread out and public transport to Carnoustie/Kingsbarns is limited
Kingsbarns Distillery is 10 min from the golf course — combine the two for a great day
A Scotland trip works best as 4-5 days to justify the travel. Don't rush it.

items.title: Arrive EDI, drive to St Andrews (90 min)
Celebration dinner at The Seafood Restaurant

destinations.kit_tagline: Walk the Old Course fairways, earn your Swilcan Bridge photo, and understand why this town owns golf history.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-June gives 16+ hours of daylight, settled weather, and avoids July tourists and Open Championship prep closures.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival round after 90-minute drive from Edinburgh. Crail is low-pressure links golf to shake off travel and dial in the ground game.
Morning start before coastal wind picks up. Best modern links in Scotland gets you links-ready before the Old Course.

recommended_itinerary.course_id: The Old Course at St Andrews
recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Prime morning slot if ballot hits. Caddies are sharp early, and you'll finish in time for the Jigger Inn ritual.
36-hole day works here. New Course is walkable Old Tom Morris links without the Old Course pressure. Usually available same-day.
Morning round at the hardest Open venue. Legs are fresh, and you need every advantage for Car-nasty.
Recovery round. Elie is charming, authentic, and forgiving after Carnoustie beat you up.
Checkout and 90-minute drive to Edinburgh. No golf unless you have a late evening flight.

recommended_lodging.name: St Andrews flat/cottage
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Group of four splits a flat for less than B&Bs and gets a kitchen for morning coffee and late-night whisky debriefs. The Scores puts you 5 minutes from the Old Course and overlooks the bay.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 6+ months out for summer dates

bonus_plays.name: Jigger Inn post-Old Course pint
bonus_plays.why: Adjacent to the 17th tee. Every golfer who's played the Old Course has had a pint here. It's not optional.

bonus_plays.name: Adamson celebration dinner
bonus_plays.why: Best restaurant in St Andrews. Reserve ahead. Worth one splurge night after you've walked the Old Course.

bonus_plays.name: Kingsbarns Distillery tour
bonus_plays.why: 10 minutes from Kingsbarns Golf Links. Combine the round and distillery for a full day. Tour takes 90 minutes.

bonus_plays.name: West Sands beach walk
bonus_plays.why: Chariots of Fire beach. Clears your head before or after rounds. 2-mile stretch of sand north of town.

destinations.avoid_reason: Brutal humidity and afternoon thunderstorms make golf miserable. Courses get stressed too.
destinations.why_go: Historic charm meets championship golf. Cobblestone streets, world-class restaurants, and Lowcountry courses with marsh views. Charleston is the thinking man's golf trip — incredible food scene after your round.

top_courses.name: Kiawah Island Ocean Course
top_courses.must_know: Host of the 2021 PGA Championship. Walking only before noon with caddie. Book as resort package to save $100+. Wind changes everything — can vary 8 clubs day to day.
top_courses.walking_policy: Walking only before noon, caddies encouraged

top_courses.name: Kiawah Island Osprey Point
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design. Most playable of the Kiawah courses. Lagoons, marsh, and maritime forest. Great warm-up round before Ocean Course.

top_courses.name: The Links at Stono Ferry
top_courses.must_know: Best value near Charleston. Former Revolutionary War site. Marsh views without the resort price tag.

top_courses.name: Patriots Point Links
top_courses.must_know: Play next to the USS Yorktown aircraft carrier. Harbor views on every hole. Short but fun — perfect arrival day round.

top_courses.name: RiverTowne Country Club
top_courses.must_know: Arnold Palmer design on the Wando River. Former Charleston Open venue. Good test without the Kiawah price tag.

hidden_gems.name: Charleston Municipal Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Oldest muni in Charleston. No frills but great bones and $25 walking rate.

hidden_gems.name: Shadowmoss Plantation
hidden_gems.must_know: Solid conditioning, surprisingly quiet. Locals' favorite value play.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah Island Golf Resort (The Sanctuary)
lodging_options.note: Full luxury. Walking distance to Ocean Course. Pool, spa, beach. Book golf packages for best rates.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah/Seabrook Island VRBO rentals
lodging_options.note: 4-6 bedroom houses. Split among 8-12 guys for great value. Still get resort golf access.

lodging_options.name: Hotel Bennett / The Vendue
lodging_options.note: Stay downtown for the restaurant scene. 30-45 min drive to Kiawah courses.

lodging_options.name: Hampton Inn Mt. Pleasant
lodging_options.note: Clean, central to both downtown and Kiawah. Good budget base.

dining.name: Husk
dining.must_know: Sean Brock's legendary Southern restaurant. Reservations essential. Menu changes daily.

dining.name: The Ordinary
dining.must_know: Best oyster bar in the South. Raw bar + craft cocktails. Great for groups.

dining.name: Rodney Scott's BBQ
dining.must_know: James Beard Award-winning whole hog BBQ. No-brainer group dinner. BYOB allowed.

dining.name: Fleet Landing
dining.must_know: Waterfront seafood on the harbor. Sunset views. Book the patio for groups.

non_golf_activities: Historic downtown walking tour (2 hrs, free-$25)
Deep sea fishing charter ($200-400/person half day)
King Street shopping and bar hopping
Shem Creek waterfront bars and restaurants
insider_tips: Play Kiawah Ocean Course on day 2 — use day 1 for a warm-up round and to adjust to the humidity.
Book a Kiawah resort package even if you're staying downtown — it saves $100+ per Ocean Course round.
Shem Creek in Mt. Pleasant is the locals' spot for post-round drinks. Skip the tourist bars on Market St.
Spring (Mar-May) has the best combo of weather and availability. Fall is peak season and books fast.
If you're a group of 8+, rent a house on Seabrook Island — half the price of Kiawah with the same beach access.

activities: Afternoon round at Patriots Point Links ($65)
Dinner at Fleet Landing on the harbor
Morning tee time at Kiawah Ocean Course ($450)
Breakfast at Callie's Hot Little Biscuit

destinations.kit_tagline: Ocean Course drama, cobblestone dinners, and marsh golf that costs half what you'd pay at Pebble.

destinations.why_go: Two Pete Dye courses in the rolling hills of southern Indiana. French Lick Resort is a historic grand hotel with casino. Dye Course hosted the Senior PGA Championship. Best golf value in the Midwest after RTJ Trail.

top_courses.name: Pete Dye Course at French Lick
top_courses.must_know: Hilltop course with 360-degree views of Hoosier National Forest. Hosted Senior PGA Championship. Walking encouraged. One of Dye's best.

top_courses.name: Donald Ross Course at French Lick
top_courses.must_know: Restored 1917 Donald Ross design. Classic golden-age architecture. More playable than the Dye Course. Both courses are on-site at the resort.

top_courses.name: Sultan's Run Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Tim Liddy design 5 min from the resort. Hilly terrain through hardwood forest. Great value addition to a French Lick trip.

hidden_gems.name: Fuzzy Zoeller's Covered Bridge
hidden_gems.must_know: Fuzzy Zoeller's home course. 15 min from French Lick. Fun, friendly, well-maintained.

lodging_options.name: French Lick Springs Hotel
lodging_options.note: Historic 1845 hotel. Casino, spa, pools. Golf packages available.

lodging_options.name: West Baden Springs Hotel
lodging_options.note: The 'Eighth Wonder of the World' — massive domed atrium. Luxury sister property.

lodging_options.name: Comfort Suites / local motels
lodging_options.note: Basic but functional. French Lick is small — everything is close.

dining.name: 1875: The Steakhouse (West Baden)
dining.must_know: Best steakhouse in southern Indiana. In the stunning West Baden hotel.

dining.name: Hagen's Club House Grill
dining.must_know: At the resort. Casual post-round dining with views.

dining.name: 33 Brick Street
dining.must_know: Downtown French Lick. Craft cocktails and pub food.

non_golf_activities: West Baden Springs Hotel dome tour (free)
insider_tips: The Pete Dye Course is brutally hard from the tips. Play the whites/blues and enjoy it.
West Baden Springs Hotel atrium is jaw-dropping — even if you stay at French Lick Springs, walk over to see it.
Book a 2-course package (Dye + Ross) for 15-20% savings.
French Lick is remote — that's the charm. Nothing to do but golf, eat, and gamble.
Fall foliage (Oct) in Hoosier National Forest makes the Dye Course otherworldly.

activities: Arrive, check into French Lick Springs

destinations.kit_tagline: Two Pete Dye masterpieces in the rolling hills of southern Indiana, with a grand hotel casino and nothing to do but golf.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-October foliage in Hoosier National Forest makes the Dye Course otherworldly, plus off-peak rates kick in.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Afternoon arrival round after lunch gives time to settle in and warm up on a forgiving track before the Dye courses.

recommended_itinerary.course_id: Pete Dye Course at French Lick
recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Early morning on the championship course when everyone's fresh and October temps are crisp for the hilltop climbs.

recommended_itinerary.course_id: Donald Ross Course at French Lick
recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Classic Ross design is more playable and forgiving after yesterday's Dye beatdown, plus later start for recovery.
Checkout and travel day, 90 min drive to Louisville or 2 hrs to Indianapolis.

recommended_lodging.name: French Lick Springs Hotel
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Historic 1845 hotel with casino, spa, and both courses on-site. Golf packages drop rates 15-20% and you never move the cars. Walk over to West Baden's dome between rounds.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 6-8 weeks out for October foliage peak and package deals.

bonus_plays.name: 1875: The Steakhouse
bonus_plays.why: Best steakhouse in southern Indiana, inside the jaw-dropping West Baden atrium. Book it for night 2 after you survive the Dye Course.

bonus_plays.name: 33 Brick Street
bonus_plays.why: Downtown French Lick craft cocktails and pub food. Low-key spot for night 1 or 3 when you don't need white tablecloths.

bonus_plays.name: West Baden Springs Hotel dome tour
bonus_plays.why: Free walk-through of the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' atrium. Takes 20 minutes and you'll understand why they call it that.

bonus_plays.name: Fuzzy Zoeller's Covered Bridge
bonus_plays.why: If you have late flights on Day 4, Fuzzy's home course is 15 min away and twilight 9 is $25. Fun closer before the airport.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 15 min from ACY, 75 min from PHL
destinations.avoid_reason: Cold, wind, many courses close.
destinations.why_go: Casino nightlife + unexpectedly good golf. AC area has several top-tier public courses including some of the best links-style in the Northeast. Play 18, hit the casino, repeat. Perfect party golf trip for the Northeast crowd.

top_courses.name: Ballamor Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Part of Atlantic City CC. Best conditioned course in the AC area. Fair test for all skill levels.

top_courses.name: Twisted Dune Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Links-style course built on Sand dunes. Feels like Scotland in New Jersey. Wind is always a factor.

top_courses.name: Shore Gate Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Ron Forse and Jim Nagle design. Good shape, fair price. Less crowded than Twisted Dune.

top_courses.name: Sand Barrens Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: 27 holes through Pine Barrens. Good group-friendly layout. Multiple nines keep it interesting.

hidden_gems.name: McCullough's Emerald Links
hidden_gems.must_know: Municipal in Egg Harbor Township. Surprisingly good for the price.

hidden_gems.name: Blue Heron Pines
hidden_gems.must_know: In Galloway. Well-maintained with pine barrens setting.

lodging_options.name: Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa
lodging_options.note: Best casino in AC. Pool, nightclubs, restaurants. Walking distance to boardwalk.

lodging_options.name: Hard Rock Hotel & Casino
lodging_options.note: Music-themed casino. Good pool scene. Group-friendly vibe.

lodging_options.name: Tropicana / Resorts Casino
lodging_options.note: Budget casino options. Still fun, just less flashy.

dining.name: Borgata's Old Homestead Steakhouse
dining.must_know: One of the best steakhouses on the East Coast. Serious meats.

dining.name: Dock's Oyster House
dining.must_know: Since 1897. Legendary AC seafood institution.

dining.name: Tony's Baltimore Grill
dining.must_know: 24-hour Italian-American diner. Post-casino 3am pizza. An AC tradition.

insider_tips: Twisted Dune is the must-play — genuine links golf near the shore. Wind makes it brutal but fun.
Borgata is the clear winner for casino/hotel quality. Worth the premium over boardwalk casinos.
Midweek casino rates drop 40-50%. Golf + gambling = Mon-Thu is the smart play.
AC is 60 min from Philly — fly into PHL for cheaper flights if needed.
Spring (May-Jun) and fall (Sep-Oct) have the best golf weather and lower hotel rates.
destinations.kit_tagline: Links golf on Jersey dunes, then casino floors until 4am. Northeast golf trip that actually parties.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-May hits the sweet spot — courses are in peak shape, casino rates are still 40% below summer, and weather is warm without July humidity.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most guys fly into PHL morning or early afternoon. Use arrival day to settle in, hit Borgata pool, then welcome dinner at Dock's.
Play Twisted Dune early before the wind cranks up. Links golf gets brutal after 11am when gusts come off the shore.
Ballamor after a casino night. Fazio design is fair and forgiving — perfect for guys nursing hangovers. Best conditions in the AC area.
Early morning round at Shore Gate, finish by noon. Gives you time for lunch and still make afternoon flights out of PHL or ACY.

recommended_lodging.name: Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Borgata is the best casino in AC by a wide margin. Pool scene, Old Homestead steakhouse, actual nightlife that doesn't feel depressing. Walking distance to boardwalk but you're not staying in a dated 1980s tower. Worth the extra $50/night over Tropicana.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · Book 8-10 weeks out. Midweek rates drop hard but rooms still sell out for group blocks in May and September.

bonus_plays.name: Tony's Baltimore Grill
bonus_plays.why: 24-hour Italian-American diner. Post-casino 3am pizza run is an AC tradition. Cheap, greasy, exactly what you need after a long table run.

bonus_plays.name: Borgata Pool Scene
bonus_plays.why: Day drinking between rounds. Pool is open May-September and the scene is solid on weekends. Better than sitting in a dark casino all afternoon.

bonus_plays.name: McCullough's Emerald Links
bonus_plays.why: Municipal in Egg Harbor. If guys want a casual 9 on arrival day, this is $40 and 15 minutes from Borgata. No pressure, just loosening up.

destinations.avoid_reason: New York winter. Cold, courses closed.
destinations.why_go: Wine country golf in upstate New York. Beautiful lake views, 100+ wineries, and surprising golf value. Perfect for the group that wants to mix rounds with wine tasting and relaxation. No pretense, just good times.

top_courses.name: The Club at Bristol Harbour
top_courses.must_know: Robert Trent Jones Sr. design on Canandaigua Lake. Stunning views. Lodge on-site for stay-and-play.

top_courses.name: Ravenwood Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Well-maintained public course near Victor. Good test without being punishing.

top_courses.name: Centennial Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: In Carmel (closer to NYC). Denis Griffiths design. Excellent conditioning for a semi-public course.

top_courses.name: Reservoir Creek Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: In Naples. Vineyard views. Basic but scenic. Great warm-up round.

hidden_gems.name: Salmon Creek Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Spencerport. Walking-friendly, well-groomed for the price.

hidden_gems.name: Mark Twain Golf Course (Elmira)
hidden_gems.must_know: State park course. Beautiful setting. 30 min drive but incredible value.

lodging_options.name: Bristol Harbour Resort
lodging_options.note: On Canandaigua Lake. On-site golf. Rooms and cabins.

lodging_options.name: The Inn at Glenora Wine Cellars
lodging_options.note: On Seneca Lake. Wine tasting on-site. Romantic but works for small groups.

lodging_options.name: Lake house VRBO rentals
lodging_options.note: Houses on Keuka, Seneca, or Canandaigua lakes. Best for groups.

dining.name: Belhurst Castle
dining.must_know: Lakefront castle restaurant on Seneca Lake. Special occasion level.

dining.name: FLX Table
dining.must_know: Chef's table experience in Geneva. 12 seats. Reservations months out.

dining.name: Simply Red Bistro
dining.must_know: Trumansburg. Farm-to-table with local wine pairings. Excellent.

non_golf_activities: Watkins Glen State Park gorge trail (free)
insider_tips: The Seneca Lake Wine Trail has 30+ tasting rooms in a 15-mile stretch. Hire a driver or van.
Bristol Harbour's 16th hole overlooking the lake is one of the prettiest in New York.
Late August/September: warm weather + grape harvest = wineries at their best.
Watkins Glen gorge trail is a must — 200-foot cliffs and 19 waterfalls in 2 miles. Free.
Group rental houses on the lakes are the move. Dock access, grills, fire pits.

activities: Arrive ROC, drive to lake house

destinations.kit_title: The Finger Lakes Golf & Wine Run
destinations.kit_tagline: Upstate wine country golf where RTJ designs meet lake views and 100+ tasting rooms between rounds.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-September hits the grape harvest season with warm weather and fewer crowds than summer peak.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: ROC arrival plus 75-minute drive makes afternoon arrival likely. Skip the forced round, settle into the house, hit range if needed.
Early morning on the signature course. That 16th hole over Canandaigua Lake is what you came for, and morning light is ideal.
Solid RTJ test without the resort premium. Morning round leaves the full afternoon open for Seneca Lake Wine Trail.
Naples location means vineyard views and a quick warm-up round. Early tee gets you to ROC by 11am for afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Lake house VRBO rentals
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Group of 6-8 splits a house for less than resort rooms, and you get dock access, grill, fire pit. Kitchen saves money on breakfasts. This is lake country—use the lake.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 3-4 months out for September dates and lake access.

bonus_plays.name: Simply Red Bistro
bonus_plays.why: Trumansburg farm-to-table with local wine pairings. Group-friendly, excellent food, and you're supporting the region's wine program.

bonus_plays.name: Watkins Glen gorge trail
bonus_plays.why: 200-foot cliffs and 19 waterfalls in 2 miles. Free. Takes 90 minutes. Do it Day 3 afternoon between wine stops.

bonus_plays.name: Finger Lakes Brewing Company
bonus_plays.why: Hammondsport location. Good beer, lake views, casual vibe for the last night before departure.
bonus_plays.when: Day 4 evening or Day 3 if you skip the castle

destinations.avoid_reason: Peak season pricing. Great weather but prices double. Book far in advance if going.
destinations.why_go: The PGA Tour's Sentry Tournament of Champions venue. Ocean-to-mountain golf on one of the most beautiful islands on Earth. Kapalua Plantation Course is bucket list. Combine with Maui's beaches, whale watching, and Road to Hana.

top_courses.name: Kapalua Plantation Course
top_courses.must_know: Host of PGA Tour's Sentry Tournament of Champions. Dramatic elevation changes with ocean views on every hole. The 18th is one of the most iconic finishing holes in golf.

top_courses.name: Kapalua Bay Course
top_courses.must_know: More playable than Plantation. Ocean views, Molokai Island backdrop. Recently redesigned.

top_courses.name: Royal Ka'anapali Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: In Ka'anapali resort area. Ocean and mountain views. More accessible than Kapalua.

top_courses.name: Wailea Gold Course
top_courses.must_know: South side of Maui. Robert Trent Jones Jr. design. Three courses at Wailea — Gold is the championship test.

hidden_gems.name: Kahili Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: In the West Maui Mountains. Less famous, less crowded, still gorgeous. Good value by Maui standards.

hidden_gems.name: Maui Nui Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Near Wailea. Renovated former Elleair course. Best budget option in South Maui.

lodging_options.name: The Ritz-Carlton Kapalua
lodging_options.note: Steps from Plantation Course. Full luxury. Pool, spa, beach access.

lodging_options.name: Montage Kapalua Bay
lodging_options.note: Luxury residences with kitchens. Perfect for groups splitting a multi-bedroom suite.

lodging_options.name: Ka'anapali condos (VRBO)
lodging_options.note: Beachfront condos in Ka'anapali. Walking distance to courses and restaurants.

dining.name: Mama's Fish House
dining.must_know: Most famous restaurant in Maui. Oceanfront. Fish caught daily. Reservations months out.

dining.name: Merriman's Kapalua
dining.must_know: Farm-to-table with ocean views. Perfect post-round sunset dinner.

dining.name: Monkeypod Kitchen
dining.must_know: Peter Merriman's casual spot. Craft cocktails, pizza, good vibes.

insider_tips: Book Plantation Course tee times the moment they open (90 days out). It sells out fast.
Shoulder season (Apr-May, Sep-Oct) has the best value: still perfect weather, 30-40% off peak rates.
Plantation Course plays 2-3 clubs downhill on many holes. Trust the elevation.
Mama's Fish House: book 2-3 months ahead. Not kidding. Or try for a walk-in lunch.
Rent a car — Uber/Lyft are unreliable on Maui. You'll need wheels for courses and restaurants.
destinations.kit_tagline: Play the Sentry venue, trust the downhill clubs, and book Mama's three months out or don't complain.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-May shoulder season delivers perfect weather at 35% off peak rates before summer crowds hit.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most mainland flights land OGG after noon. Use afternoon for beach and settling in at Kapalua.
First full day on the bucket list course. Morning tee before wind picks up and while legs are fresh for elevation changes.
South side drive from Kapalua is 90 minutes. Early start gets you there by 9am for warm-up, handles travel, and leaves afternoon for pool.
Easier RTJ Sr. layout for final round when bodies are tired. Early finish allows checkout and OGG departure by 2pm.

recommended_lodging.name: Montage Kapalua Bay
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Multi-bedroom residences with full kitchens let groups of 6-8 split costs and save $15-20/person/day on breakfasts. Walking distance to Plantation Course and better bathroom ratio than cramming into hotel rooms.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 4-6 months out for shoulder season, 6-9 months for winter.

bonus_plays.name: Mama's Fish House
