bonus_plays.why: Most famous restaurant on Maui. Oceanfront, fish caught that day. Book 2-3 months ahead or try walk-in lunch. Not kidding about the lead time.

bonus_plays.name: Merriman's Kapalua
bonus_plays.why: Farm-to-table with ocean views. Perfect post-Plantation celebration dinner at sunset. Walking distance from Montage.

bonus_plays.name: Kapalua Bay Course twilight
bonus_plays.why: If group wants more golf, Bay Course twilight at $139 is the move. More playable than Plantation, same ocean views, Molokai backdrop.

bonus_plays.name: Honolua Bay snorkeling
bonus_plays.why: Free. Ten minutes from Kapalua. Best snorkeling on the island. Go morning of Day 3 before driving to Wailea.
bonus_plays.when: Day 3 morning before Wailea tee time

destinations.avoid_reason: Hurricane season. Heavy rains, some courses temporarily close.
destinations.why_go: All-inclusive resorts with golf included. Caribbean beaches, cenotes, ancient ruins, and nightlife. Your dollar goes 2-3x farther in Mexico. Jack Nicklaus designed El Camaleon hosts the PGA Tour.

top_courses.name: El Camaleon Golf Course (Mayakoba)
top_courses.must_know: Host of PGA Tour's World Wide Technology Championship. Greg Norman design through jungle, mangroves, and Caribbean coast. One hole plays along the beach.

top_courses.name: Playa Mujeres Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Greg Norman design north of Cancun. Ocean views and mangroves. Part of Dreams resort complex.

top_courses.name: Iberostar Playa Paraiso Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: P.B. Dye design in the jungle. Cenotes on the course. Part of Iberostar all-inclusive — guests get discounted rates.

top_courses.name: Puerto Cancun Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Tom Weiskopf design right in Cancun hotel zone. Lagoon and mangrove scenery. Convenient if staying in Cancun.

hidden_gems.name: Riviera Cancun Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design. Less crowded than El Camaleon. Good value.

hidden_gems.name: Hard Rock Golf Club Riviera Maya
hidden_gems.must_know: Robert von Hagge design. Connected to Hard Rock all-inclusive.

lodging_options.name: Mayakoba resorts (Fairmont/Rosewood/Banyan Tree)
lodging_options.note: Luxury all-inclusive with El Camaleon access. Pool, beach, spa, food/drinks included.

lodging_options.name: Iberostar Selection Paraiso
lodging_options.note: Great mid-range all-inclusive. On-site golf. Large group-friendly.

lodging_options.name: Cancun Hotel Zone all-inclusives
lodging_options.note: Dozens of options. Beach, pools, nightlife. Book golf separately.

dining.name: All-inclusive restaurants
dining.must_know: Most stays are all-inclusive so dining is covered. Quality varies by resort — Mayakoba resorts have the best food.

dining.name: La Fisheria (Playa del Carmen)
dining.must_know: Best seafood on 5th Avenue. Ceviche is incredible.

dining.name: Porfirio's (Cancun)
dining.must_know: Upscale Mexican cuisine. If you leave the resort for one dinner, make it this.

insider_tips: All-inclusive is the move for groups. Food, drinks, and often golf included. Do the math — it's almost always cheaper.
El Camaleon is the prestige course, but Iberostar gives 80% of the experience at half the price.
Playa del Carmen has better nightlife than Cancun hotel zone for younger groups. 5th Avenue is walkable.
Dollar goes far: caddie tips, drinks, dinners off-resort are all 40-60% cheaper than US equivalents.
Hurricane season is Aug-Oct. Insurance is worth it. Nov-Apr is perfect weather.
destinations.kit_tagline: All-inclusive resorts, PGA Tour course, and your dollar stretched twice as far on the Yucatan.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-February hits peak weather window without spring break pricing or crowds.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most flights land CUN by early afternoon. Settle into resort, hit the beach, save energy for El Camaleon tomorrow.
Morning start before Caribbean heat peaks. This is the showcase round—play it fresh and early.
Another morning round to beat heat. Cenotes and jungle make this course play cooler than exposed layouts.
Early tee for last round. Most afternoon flights give you time for 18, lunch, and transfer to CUN by 1pm.

recommended_lodging.name: Iberostar Selection Paraiso
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: On-site golf, all-inclusive food and drinks covered, and mid-range pricing that leaves budget for El Camaleon. Groups of 8-16 get the best value here without sacrificing quality.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 60-90 days out. Peak season fills early and rates climb closer to travel dates.

bonus_plays.name: Playa del Carmen 5th Avenue
bonus_plays.why: Better nightlife than Cancun hotel zone for groups under 40. Walkable bars, clubs, and street life. Your dollar stretches—drinks and cover are half US prices.

bonus_plays.name: Cenote swimming
bonus_plays.why: Natural limestone sinkholes with crystal-clear water. Free to $25 depending on location. Stop at Dos Ojos or Gran Cenote on the way back from Iberostar.

bonus_plays.name: Porfirio's (Cancun)
bonus_plays.why: If you leave the resort for one dinner, make it this. Upscale Mexican that's still cheaper than any steakhouse back home.

destinations.avoid_reason: Hurricane season. Heat and heavy rain.
destinations.why_go: Caribbean all-inclusive + world-class golf at unbeatable prices. Multiple Jack Nicklaus and P.B. Dye designs with ocean holes. Your dollar stretches far. Perfect bachelor party or buddy trip.

top_courses.name: Punta Espada Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design at Cap Cana. 8 holes on the Caribbean. #1 course in the Caribbean and Latin America by Golf Digest. The Pebble Beach of the Caribbean.

top_courses.name: Corales Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design at Puntacana Resort. Host of PGA Tour's Corales Championship. Six holes along coral cliffs. The 'Devil's Elbow' finish is legendary.

top_courses.name: La Cana Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: P.B. Dye design at Puntacana Resort. 27 holes. More playable than Corales. Ocean views on several holes.

top_courses.name: Iberostar Bavaro Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: P.B. Dye design at Iberostar all-inclusive. Guests get discounted rates. Good value included in some packages.

hidden_gems.name: Catalonia Caribe Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Newer Alberto Sola design. Less famous, lower cost, still good.

lodging_options.name: Puntacana Resort & Club
lodging_options.note: Three courses on-site. Beach, spa, restaurants. The premier golf resort.

lodging_options.name: Iberostar Selection Bavaro
lodging_options.note: On-site golf. Large group-friendly. Great value all-inclusive.

lodging_options.name: Hard Rock Hotel Punta Cana
lodging_options.note: Party all-inclusive. Casino, nightclub, pool scene.

dining.name: All-inclusive dining
dining.must_know: All-inclusive covers most meals. Puntacana Resort has best restaurant variety.

dining.name: La Yola
dining.must_know: At Puntacana Marina. Fresh seafood, water views. Worth leaving the resort.

insider_tips: Punta Espada is the must-play. Budget for it even if you play cheaper courses the other days.
All-inclusive math: room + unlimited food/drinks + golf discounts = always better value than booking separately.
Caddie tips are cheap by US standards — $30-40 per bag is generous and appreciated.
Hard Rock is the bachelor party resort. Puntacana Resort is the golf-focused option.
Flights from East Coast are 3-4 hours direct. Easier than you think.
destinations.kit_tagline: Three Jack Nicklaus-class courses, unlimited rum, and oceanside golf for less than a Pinehurst weekend.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-February hits peak weather without spring break pricing. East Coast flights are plentiful.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most East Coast flights land 2-4pm. Check in, hit the pool, settle the room situations.
Play the Caribbean's #1 course when you're fresh. Morning gets you off before wind picks up on ocean holes.
PGA Tour venue second. Devil's Elbow finish is iconic. Afternoon open for catamaran or beach recovery.
Most forgiving of the three. Early start gets you to airport by 1pm for afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Iberostar Selection Bavaro
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: All-inclusive math works best here. Unlimited food and drinks included, on-site golf gets you discounts at other courses, and it handles groups of 8-16 without thinking twice. Hard Rock is more party, Puntacana is more premium—this is the sweet spot.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 90 days out. All-inclusives fill early February-March.

bonus_plays.name: La Yola
bonus_plays.why: Only off-resort meal worth it. Fresh catch at Puntacana Marina. Get a table at sunset day 2 or 3.

bonus_plays.name: Catamaran cruise
bonus_plays.why: Day 3 afternoon while the resort golfers are stuck playing their on-site course. Open bar, snorkeling, zero effort.

bonus_plays.name: Resort casino
bonus_plays.why: Blackjack and cigars after dinner. Iberostar casino is solid, Hard Rock is bigger if you want to Uber over.

destinations.avoid_reason: Peak summer heat (90F+) and peak European tourist season. Crowded and expensive.
destinations.why_go: Europe's premier golf destination. 40+ courses along the sunny south coast of Portugal. Clifftop ocean holes, world-class resorts, incredible food and wine at European prices. Direct flights from East Coast hubs.

top_courses.name: Monte Rei North Course
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design. #1 course in Portugal. Immaculate conditioning. Eastern Algarve near the Spanish border.

top_courses.name: Quinta do Lago South
top_courses.must_know: Three courses at Quinta do Lago. South is the championship test — hosted Portuguese Open multiple times. Pine forests and lagoon views.

top_courses.name: San Lorenzo Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Adjacent to Quinta do Lago. Ria Formosa wetlands setting. One of Europe's most beautiful courses. Flamingos on the course.

top_courses.name: Vale do Lobo Royal
top_courses.must_know: The iconic clifftop par-3 16th over red cliffs to the sea. Most photographed hole in European golf.

hidden_gems.name: Amendoeira Faldo Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Nick Faldo design inland. Surprisingly good for the price. Less crowded.

hidden_gems.name: Silves Golf
hidden_gems.must_know: Inland course near historic Silves castle. Great budget option.

lodging_options.name: Conrad Algarve (Quinta do Lago)
lodging_options.note: Luxury resort. Walking distance to Quinta courses. Pool, spa, restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Pine Cliffs Resort
lodging_options.note: 9-hole clifftop course on-site. Near Albufeira. Full resort amenities.

lodging_options.name: Algarve villa rentals
lodging_options.note: Private villas with pools. Best for groups of 6+. Private chef available.

dining.name: Gusto by Heinz Beck
dining.must_know: Michelin-starred at Conrad. Mediterranean fine dining.

dining.name: A Ria (Faro)
dining.must_know: Fresh seafood on the Ria Formosa. Local institution. Grilled fish is incredible.

dining.name: Noélia & Jerónimo (Cabanas)
dining.must_know: Simple beachside grilled fish restaurant. One of the best meals you'll have anywhere.

non_golf_activities: Beach day at Praia da Marinha (free)
Lagos old town and cliff walks
Faro old town and Ria Formosa boat trip
insider_tips: Book a golf passport: multi-course packages save 20-30% vs. individual green fees.
Spring (Mar-May) and fall (Sep-Nov) are the sweet spots: warm, affordable, less crowded.
Vale do Lobo #16: take a photo before you hit. The cliff backdrop is unreal regardless of your score.
Portuguese wine is criminally underrated. €5-10 bottles rival $30-40 bottles from France/California.
Fly into Faro (FAO) — direct flights from London, other EU hubs. East Coast flights connect through Lisbon.
The food in the Algarve is some of the best value in Europe. Full seafood dinner for €15-25/person.
destinations.kit_tagline: Four championship courses along Portugal's southern coast where the greens fees are half what you'd pay at home.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-April hits the spring sweet spot: 70-75F temps, low crowds, off-peak pricing before summer rates kick in.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most East Coast connections through Lisbon land in Faro mid-afternoon. Check in, settle, hit range if energy allows.
Start with the most beautiful course in the region while the group is fresh. Flamingos are most active in morning light.
Get to #16 by mid-morning for ideal photo light on the clifftop hole. Earlier tee time before April winds pick up.
Championship test on the final day. Slightly later start allows for recovery from previous two days.
Early departure round for late afternoon flights. The Nicklaus masterpiece deserves fresh legs and empty fairways.

recommended_lodging.name: Algarve villa rentals
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: For groups of 8, splitting a villa at €250/night beats resort rooms every time. Private pool, kitchen for breakfast saves €15/person/day, and you're central to all four courses.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 90-120 days out. Spring villas book early, especially for groups.

bonus_plays.name: Noélia & Jerónimo
bonus_plays.why: Drive 40 minutes east to Cabanas for the simplest, best grilled fish you'll ever eat. Order whatever came in that morning and a bottle of vinho verde.
bonus_plays.when: Day 3 evening after Vale do Lobo

bonus_plays.name: Amendoeira Faldo Course
bonus_plays.why: If someone's flight doesn't leave until evening on Day 5, the Faldo course is 20 minutes from the airport and €60-80 for 18. Solid backup plan.

bonus_plays.name: Golf passport booking
bonus_plays.why: Book through Algarve golf passport programs before you go. Four rounds pre-paid saves 20-25% versus walk-up rates at these courses.

destinations.avoid_reason: Short days, cold, rain. Courses playable but conditions are rough.
destinations.why_go: The birthplace of links golf. Ballybunion, Lahinch, Tralee, and Waterville are all within driving distance in County Kerry and Clare. Pubs with live music, Guinness, and the most dramatic coastal golf on Earth.

top_courses.name: Ballybunion (Old Course)
top_courses.must_know: One of the greatest links courses ever built. Towering sand dunes, Atlantic views. Walking only. Tom Watson called it the best links course he's ever played.

top_courses.name: Lahinch Golf Club (Old Course)
top_courses.must_know: The 'St. Andrews of Ireland.' Overlooking Liscannor Bay. Iconic Goat Tower. The Dell hole (#5) is blind and unforgettable.

top_courses.name: Tralee Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Arnold Palmer's only European design. Dramatic ocean cliff holes. Back nine is some of the most spectacular golf anywhere. Very difficult in wind.

top_courses.name: Waterville Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: On the Ring of Kerry. Classic links in a remote, stunning setting. Payne Stewart statue at the 1st tee. Less crowded than Ballybunion.

hidden_gems.name: Dooks Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Old links course overlooking Dingle Bay. Charming, authentic, affordable.

hidden_gems.name: Ceann Sibéal (Dingle)
hidden_gems.must_know: Westernmost golf course in Europe. Dramatic cliffs. Star Wars was filmed nearby.

lodging_options.name: The Europe Hotel & Resort (Killarney)
lodging_options.note: Luxury lakeside hotel. Central base for all courses. Spa, restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Traditional B&Bs (various)
lodging_options.note: The Irish experience. Full Irish breakfast. Pub walking distance. Book individual rooms.

lodging_options.name: Dingle Skellig Hotel
lodging_options.note: In Dingle town. Pool, spa. Great base for Dingle Peninsula courses.

dining.name: Local pubs (every town)
dining.must_know: Irish pubs are the dining experience. Fresh seafood, lamb stew, Guinness. Live music most nights.

dining.name: The Chart House (Dingle)
dining.must_know: Best restaurant in Dingle. Seafood-focused. Reservations recommended.

dining.name: Lord Baker's (Dingle)
dining.must_know: Pub food and pints. Great craic (fun). Live trad music.

non_golf_activities: Ring of Kerry drive (full day, free)
insider_tips: Bring rain gear for every round. Seriously. It will rain. It will also be sunny. Often in the same hour.
Walking is the only option and the only way to play links golf. Get a pull trolley if you don't use a caddie.
Ballybunion books up 3 months out in summer. Don't delay.
Irish pubs are the real cultural experience. Skip fancy restaurants — eat in pubs.
Rent a car and embrace driving on the left. Roads are narrow but manageable. Buses don't reach the courses.
May and September offer the best combo of weather, daylight, and lower prices.

activities: Dooks Golf Club (€80) or rest day

destinations.kit_tagline: Four of Ireland's greatest links courses in County Kerry and Clare, with pubs and Guinness between rounds.

default_recommended_dates.reason: May offers long daylight, lower prices than peak summer, and courses before the July rush hits Ballybunion.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Afternoon tee after landing at Shannon and 50-minute drive to Lahinch. Easier opener than Ballybunion.
Early morning on the best course of the trip. Walking only, so start before afternoon wind picks up off the Atlantic.
Morning start for Arnold Palmer's dramatic back nine cliffs. Very hard in wind, so avoid afternoon gusts.
Early round on the Ring of Kerry before 90-minute drive back to Shannon for afternoon departure.

recommended_lodging.name: Traditional B&Bs (various)
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: The actual Irish experience. Full breakfast included, pub within walking distance, and you'll pay half what the Europe Hotel charges. Book individual rooms in Ballybunion or Dingle depending on routing.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Moderate · 60 days out for summer, flexible otherwise

bonus_plays.name: Local pubs (every town)
bonus_plays.why: Irish pubs are the dining experience. Fresh seafood, lamb stew, Guinness, and live trad music most nights. Skip fancy restaurants.

bonus_plays.name: Dooks Golf Club
bonus_plays.why: Old links course overlooking Dingle Bay. Charming, authentic, affordable at €60-100. Perfect for a Day 3 afternoon if the group has gas left.

bonus_plays.name: Cliffs of Moher
bonus_plays.why: 20-minute detour from Lahinch. Eight-dollar entry. Do it on Day 1 before or after your round while you're right there.

bonus_plays.name: Lord Baker's (Dingle)
bonus_plays.why: Pub food, pints, and live trad music. Great craic. If you stay in Dingle, this is the spot.

destinations.avoid_reason: June Gloom — marine layer means fog until noon. Golf is fine but gray.
destinations.why_go: Municipal golf at a US Open venue overlooking the Pacific. Torrey Pines South is the best municipal course in America — hosted Tiger's famous 2008 US Open. La Jolla's restaurants and beaches complete the trip.

top_courses.name: Torrey Pines (South Course)
top_courses.must_know: Host of 2008 and 2021 US Opens and annual PGA Tour Farmers Insurance Open. Ocean cliff views. San Diego residents get discounted rates ($100). Non-residents pay $202-275. Book via lottery system 7 days in advance.

top_courses.name: Torrey Pines (North Course)
top_courses.must_know: More playable than South. Same ocean views. Recently renovated by Tom Weiskopf. Great warm-up if playing South the next day.

top_courses.name: Maderas Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Best private-quality course open to public in San Diego. 30 min north. Excellent conditioning year-round.

hidden_gems.name: Balboa Park Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: San Diego's beloved muni. Walking-friendly. Downtown views. Classic.

hidden_gems.name: Coronado Municipal Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Oceanside muni on Coronado Island. Views of downtown and the bridge.

lodging_options.name: The Lodge at Torrey Pines
lodging_options.note: Adjacent to Torrey Pines. Craftsman luxury. Spa, A.R. Valentien restaurant.

lodging_options.name: La Jolla Shores Hotel
lodging_options.note: Beachfront. Walking distance to La Jolla village. 10 min to Torrey Pines.

lodging_options.name: Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines
lodging_options.note: Overlooking Torrey Pines. Pool, restaurant. Good mid-range.

dining.name: A.R. Valentien (Lodge at Torrey Pines)
dining.must_know: Farm-to-table at the Lodge. Best restaurant in La Jolla.

dining.name: George's at the Cove
dining.must_know: Ocean-view rooftop. La Jolla institution. Get the Ocean Terrace for casual.

dining.name: Taco Stand
dining.must_know: Best fish tacos in La Jolla. Cash only. Line out the door. Worth it.

non_golf_activities: Beach day at La Jolla Shores (free)
Craft brewery tour — San Diego has 150+ ($15-30 tastings)
insider_tips: Book Torrey Pines through the online lottery system exactly 7 days in advance. Set an alarm.
If you can't get a South Course time, book North and add your name to the South standby list at the pro shop.
San Diego residents pay $100 for South Course. If anyone in your group lives there, book under their name.
The marine layer burns off by noon most days. Afternoon rounds often have better weather and views.
La Jolla has the best combo of golf + dining + beach in California. Better than Pebble Beach area for a group.

activities: Arrive SAN, check into La Jolla

destinations.kit_tagline: Municipal golf at a US Open venue with ocean cliff views, then fish tacos and craft beer in La Jolla.

default_recommended_dates.reason: October sits in the best weather window after marine layer season ends and before holiday pricing kicks in.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Afternoon arrival from SAN means late tee time. Marine layer burns off by then and North is the easier warm-up.
Early morning for the main event. Get through the difficult front nine before energy drops and wind picks up.
Morning tee time leaves afternoon free for La Jolla Cove or beach. Maderas conditions stay excellent all day.
Checkout and brunch before afternoon flights. No golf unless you have a late departure.

recommended_lodging.name: Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Overlooks Torrey Pines courses with pool and on-site restaurant. Best value for groups that want proximity to golf without Lodge pricing. Ten minutes to La Jolla village for dinners.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Medium priority · 2-3 months out for October dates

bonus_plays.name: George's at the Cove Ocean Terrace
bonus_plays.why: Ocean views at sunset after the South Course round. The Ocean Terrace level is casual enough for golf clothes and won't blow the budget like the main dining room.

bonus_plays.name: Taco Stand
bonus_plays.why: Best fish tacos in La Jolla. Cash only. Line moves fast. Order the smoked fish taco and the battered mahi. Pair with a brewery crawl after.

bonus_plays.name: La Jolla Cove kayaking or snorkeling
bonus_plays.why: Post-Maderas afternoon activity. Rentals are 50 bucks. The sea caves and leopard sharks make it worth the paddle. Better than sitting at the pool.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 15 min from MDT, 2 hrs from PHL
destinations.avoid_reason: Cold Pennsylvania winter. Some courses close.
destinations.why_go: The Sweetest Place on Earth has surprisingly excellent golf. Hershey Country Club courses have hosted PGA Tour events. Hotel Hershey is a grand resort with chocolate spa treatments. Perfect for father-son or family-friendly golf trips with non-golf entertainment.

top_courses.name: Hershey Country Club (East Course)
top_courses.must_know: George Fazio design. Former LPGA Championship venue. Resort guests get access. Best conditioning in the region.

top_courses.name: Hershey Country Club (West Course)
top_courses.must_know: Maurice McCarthy design. Classic layout through rolling Pennsylvania hills. More playable than East.

top_courses.name: Hershey Links
top_courses.must_know: 9-hole par-3 course and full 18-hole layout. Good warm-up or family-friendly option.

top_courses.name: Royal Oaks Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: 15 min from Hershey. Public course with a resort feel. Good budget option.

hidden_gems.name: Iron Valley Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: In Cornwall. P.B. Dye design. Dramatically underpriced for the quality.

hidden_gems.name: Blue Mountain Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Mountain setting 20 min north. Views and value.

lodging_options.name: Hotel Hershey
lodging_options.note: Grand 1933 hotel. Chocolate spa, formal gardens, pool. Golf packages available.

lodging_options.name: Hershey Lodge
lodging_options.note: More casual than Hotel Hershey. Indoor water park, restaurants. Better for families.

lodging_options.name: Hampton Inn / local hotels
lodging_options.note: Standard chains near the park. Functional and affordable.

dining.name: The Circular (Hotel Hershey)
dining.must_know: Fine dining in the grand hotel. Sunday brunch is legendary.

dining.name: Hershey Grill
dining.must_know: At Hershey Lodge. Casual American fare. Good post-round spot.

dining.name: What-A-Burger
dining.must_know: Local chain since 1957. Not Whataburger — unique to Hershey. Milkshakes.

insider_tips: Hotel Hershey golf packages bundle 2 courses + lodging and save 15-20%.
The Chocolate Spa sounds gimmicky but it's actually excellent. Chocolate body wrap = serious relaxation.
Fall foliage (Oct) makes the East Course stunning. Book early for peak color.
Troegs Brewery is 10 min away and one of the best craft breweries in the Mid-Atlantic.
If anyone has kids, Hersheypark makes this the easiest 'golf trip with family' sell.
destinations.kit_tagline: Championship golf where Milton Hershey built his empire. Former LPGA venue, chocolate spa, and zero logistical friction.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-September hits peak weather with smaller crowds after Labor Day. October foliage dates book early and cost more.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most flights into MDT land by 2pm. Use afternoon for check-in and range time at Hotel Hershey facilities.
Play the harder East Course first when energy is high. Early tee gets you done by lunch before any afternoon wind.
More playable West layout lets guys relax day 2. Later tee since no one needs extra warm-up after yesterday.
Early departure round at Royal Oaks. Ron Forse design has resort feel at public pricing. Done by noon for checkout and MDT flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Hotel Hershey
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Golf packages bundle East and West access with lodging and save 15-20%. You're here for the courses, so stay where they are. The 1933 grand hotel vibe makes this feel like a real trip, not a Hampton weekend.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 6-8 weeks out for September. October foliage dates need 3+ months.

bonus_plays.name: Troegs Brewing Company
bonus_plays.why: 10 minutes from Hotel Hershey and one of the best craft breweries in the Mid-Atlantic. Tour is cheap or free. The Perpetual IPA is mandatory.

bonus_plays.name: The Circular Sunday Brunch
bonus_plays.why: If your trip lands on a Sunday, the brunch at The Circular is legendary. Worth adjusting dates for. Fine dining in the grand hotel without the dinner formality.

bonus_plays.name: Chocolate Spa
bonus_plays.why: Sounds gimmicky but it's actually excellent. Chocolate body wrap is serious relaxation. Wives will ask why you went without them.

bonus_plays.name: What-A-Burger
bonus_plays.why: Local chain since 1957. Not the Texas Whataburger. Unique to Hershey. Milkshakes are the move. Good last-night casual spot.

destinations.avoid_reason: Michigan winter. Courses closed.
destinations.why_go: Best craft beer city in America + excellent affordable golf. Lake Michigan dune courses, great public options, and you'll spend half what you would at most destination trips. The Midwest's best-kept golf secret.

top_courses.name: Arcadia Bluffs (Bluffs Course)
top_courses.must_know: Perched on 200-foot bluffs over Lake Michigan. Links-style with ocean-like views. Walking only. 90 min from GR but absolutely must-play. One of the best public courses in America.

top_courses.name: Arcadia Bluffs (South Course)
top_courses.must_know: Dana Fry & Jason Straka design. Inland links through dunes and wetlands. Walking only. Complements the Bluffs Course beautifully.

top_courses.name: Thousand Oaks Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Best value in the Grand Rapids area. Well-maintained. Good test without being punishing.

top_courses.name: Tullymore Golf Resort
top_courses.must_know: Jim Engh design. 45 min from GR. 36 holes (Tullymore + St. Ives). Dramatic elevation changes through northern Michigan forest. Stay-and-play available.

hidden_gems.name: The Meadows at GVSU
hidden_gems.must_know: University course. Michael Hurdzan design. Absurd value for the quality.

hidden_gems.name: Ravines Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Arnold Palmer design in Saugatuck. Deep ravines, elevation, character.

lodging_options.name: Amway Grand Plaza Hotel
lodging_options.note: Downtown GR. Walking distance to breweries. Historic hotel.

lodging_options.name: Tullymore Golf Resort
lodging_options.note: On-site at Tullymore. Cottages and lodge rooms. 36 holes of golf.

lodging_options.name: Hampton Inn / Courtyard GR
lodging_options.note: Standard chains. Central location. Clean and reliable.

dining.name: Founders Brewing Co.
dining.must_know: One of the most famous craft breweries in America. Taproom + restaurant. KBS and All Day IPA.

dining.name: Brewery Vivant
dining.must_know: Belgian-style brewery in a converted chapel. Outstanding food and beer.

dining.name: San Chez Bistro
dining.must_know: Best restaurant in downtown GR. Tapas-style. Great for groups.

non_golf_activities: Grand Rapids Beer City Ale Trail (free passport)
Lake Michigan beach day at Holland/Saugatuck
insider_tips: Arcadia Bluffs is 90 min drive but non-negotiable. Some call it a 'poor man's Bandon Dunes.' They're wrong — it's its own masterpiece.
Grand Rapids has 80+ breweries. The Ale Trail passport rewards you for visiting them. Bring a designated driver.
July and August are Michigan summer — perfect weather, long days, Lake Michigan is warm enough to swim.
Book Arcadia early. Weekends sell out fast in summer.
Make it a road trip: GR breweries + Tullymore + Arcadia Bluffs = the ultimate Midwest golf trip.

activities: Arrive GRR, check into downtown GR
Brunch at San Chez, depart GRR

destinations.kit_tagline: Lake Michigan clifftop golf and America's best brewery scene at half the cost of coastal destinations.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-June hits peak Michigan summer weather without July weekend crowds at Arcadia Bluffs.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival round after morning flights. Moderate difficulty shakes out travel rust without punishing the group.
Early start for the 90-min drive north. Morning tee before Lake Michigan wind picks up on the bluffs.
Stay overnight near Arcadia. Morning round on the South Course before driving back to Grand Rapids.
Early departure round. Jim Engh drama through the forest, done by noon for afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Hampton Inn / Courtyard GR
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Downtown location puts you walking distance to Founders and Brewery Vivant. Two nights here, one night near Arcadia splits the drive and keeps costs reasonable.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Standard · 2-3 weeks out is fine

bonus_plays.name: Founders Brewing Co.
bonus_plays.why: Day 1 welcome dinner at one of America's most famous craft breweries. KBS on tap if you're lucky.

bonus_plays.name: Grand Rapids Ale Trail
bonus_plays.why: Free passport rewards you for hitting multiple breweries. 80+ options. Designate a driver or Uber between stops.

bonus_plays.name: San Chez Bistro
bonus_plays.why: Best restaurant downtown. Tapas format works perfectly for groups. Book the farewell dinner here.

bonus_plays.name: The Meadows at GVSU
bonus_plays.why: If someone's flight is late Day 1, skip Thousand Oaks and play this Hurdzan design instead. Absurd value at $35.

destinations.nearest_airport: LIT (Little Rock) or XNA (Northwest Arkansas Regional)
destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 60 min from LIT to Hot Springs
destinations.avoid_reason: Arkansas summer heat and humidity. 95F+.
destinations.why_go: Possibly the best golf value in America outside the RTJ Trail. Hot Springs Village has 9(!) courses, all beautiful Ozark mountain layouts at absurdly low prices. Add in Oaklawn Racing & Casino, bathhouse row, and brewery scene. Nobody talks about Arkansas golf and that's what makes it great.

top_courses.name: Hot Springs Village (Balboa)
top_courses.must_know: Best of the 9 HSV courses. Edmund Ault design through mountain forest. Elevation changes, creek crossings, stunning Ozark views. $30-60 for this quality is criminal.

top_courses.name: Hot Springs Village (Isabella)
top_courses.must_know: Gene Bates design. Most playable of the HSV courses. Beautiful lake and mountain views.

top_courses.name: Alotian Club
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design. One of the most exclusive clubs in the South. Hosted Walker Cup. If you can get an invite, take it. Otherwise, dream.

top_courses.name: Stonebridge Meadows (Fayetteville)
top_courses.must_know: In NW Arkansas. Good value public course. Well-maintained.

hidden_gems.name: Big Creek Golf & Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Mountain Home area. Beautiful Ozark setting. Incredible value.

hidden_gems.name: Mystic Creek Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: El Dorado. Newer Davis Love III design. Under the radar.

lodging_options.name: Hot Springs Village rentals/lodges
lodging_options.note: Vacation homes inside the Village. Walk to courses. Full kitchens.

lodging_options.name: Hotel & Spa at Hot Springs
lodging_options.note: Downtown Hot Springs on Bathhouse Row. Thermal baths, spa.

lodging_options.name: Hampton Inn Hot Springs
lodging_options.note: Clean, central, affordable. Typical chain quality.

dining.name: McClard's Bar-B-Q
dining.must_know: Bill Clinton's favorite BBQ joint. Since 1928. Ribs and tamales. A must.

dining.name: Superior Bathhouse Brewery
dining.must_know: Only brewery in a national park. Brewed with Hot Springs thermal water. Unique.

dining.name: Rolando's Restaurante
dining.must_know: Best Latin food in Hot Springs. James Beard nominated.

insider_tips: Hot Springs Village visitor passes give access to all 9 courses. Play 3-4 in a trip at $30-60 each. Insane value.
Oaklawn Casino has thoroughbred racing Jan-May. If timing works, it's a blast.
McClard's BBQ is cash only and closes early. Plan accordingly.
The thermal baths on Bathhouse Row are legit therapeutic. Perfect recovery day between rounds.
Northwest Arkansas (Fayetteville/Bentonville) is a separate trip worth making — Crystal Bridges museum + great golf.
Everything in Arkansas is cheap. Dinner for 8 at a nice restaurant runs $200-300 total.

activities: Arrive LIT, drive to Hot Springs (60 min)

destinations.kit_tagline: Nine mountain courses under $60, thermal baths between rounds, and nobody else knows about it yet.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-April hits peak spring conditions before summer heat. Oaklawn racing still running.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: 60-minute drive from LIT arrival. Use afternoon to settle into Hot Springs Village and hit the range.
Best of the 9 HSV courses. Morning start before any afternoon wind on the elevated holes.
Most playable layout. Morning round leaves afternoon open for Bathhouse Row recovery.
Early departure round. DeSoto is closest to village lodging and finishes by 11:30am for checkout.
Checkout and 60-minute drive to LIT. No golf scheduled.

recommended_lodging.name: Hot Springs Village rentals/lodges
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Inside the Village puts you walking distance to all 9 courses. Full kitchen saves $15-20/person/day on breakfasts. For 8 guys, splitting a house at $175/night is $22/person versus $120 hotel rooms.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Book 2-3 months out. Village rentals fill up during spring season.

bonus_plays.name: McClard's Bar-B-Q
bonus_plays.why: Bill Clinton's favorite BBQ since 1928. Ribs and tamales are mandatory. Cash only and closes early, so plan for Day 2 late lunch.

bonus_plays.name: Superior Bathhouse Brewery
bonus_plays.why: Only brewery in a national park. Beers brewed with thermal spring water. Weird and worth it.

bonus_plays.name: Oaklawn Racing & Casino
bonus_plays.why: Thoroughbred racing runs through April. Free entry, cheap drinks, $2 exactas. Perfect post-round activity.

bonus_plays.name: Bathhouse Row thermal baths
bonus_plays.why: Legit therapeutic recovery between rounds. $40-75 gets you the full soak and steam treatment.

destinations.avoid_reason: North Carolina summer heat and humidity.
destinations.why_go: The Golf Capital of the World — and it earns the title. Pinehurst No. 2 is hosting the 2024 US Open (men's and women's). 40+ courses in a 15-mile radius. Stay at the resort and play 3-4 different Pinehurst courses, then supplement with the outstanding public and semi-private options around Southern Pines.

top_courses.name: Pinehurst No. 2
top_courses.must_know: The cathedral of American golf. Host of multiple US Opens. Donald Ross's masterpiece, restored by Coore/Crenshaw in 2011 with native sand areas and wire grass. Caddie strongly recommended ($60+tip). Must stay at resort to play.

top_courses.name: Pinehurst No. 4
top_courses.must_know: Gil Hanse redesign (2018). Many consider it the best playing experience at Pinehurst now. Wide fairways, strategic bunkering, incredible greens. Host of 2019 US Amateur.

top_courses.name: Tobacco Road
top_courses.must_know: Mike Strantz's wild, divisive masterpiece. Blind shots, massive sand waste areas, love-it-or-hate-it design. 20 min from Pinehurst. Not for everyone but unforgettable.

top_courses.name: Mid Pines Inn & Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Donald Ross design restored by Kyle Franz. Sister course to Pine Needles. Classic golden-age golf. Intimate boutique resort feel.

top_courses.name: Pine Needles Lodge & Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Donald Ross design. Hosted 3 US Women's Opens. Sister to Mid Pines. Walking encouraged. Beautiful club with the Peggy Kirk Bell legacy.

hidden_gems.name: Talamore Golf Resort
hidden_gems.must_know: Rees Jones design. Great conditioning for the price. Llama caddies used to be a thing.

hidden_gems.name: Dormie Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Coore/Crenshaw design. Walking only. Members club but limited public play. If you can get on, do it.

lodging_options.name: Pinehurst Resort (Carolina Hotel)
lodging_options.note: The grand hotel. Walking distance to No. 2. Full resort with 9 courses, spa, restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Mid Pines Inn
lodging_options.note: Intimate 1921 Donald Ross era inn. On-site course. Old-school charm.

lodging_options.name: Pine Needles Lodge
lodging_options.note: Lodge with on-site Ross course. Golf packages. Great value for the quality.

lodging_options.name: Hampton Inn Southern Pines
lodging_options.note: Standard chain 10 min from Pinehurst. Saves money for green fees.

dining.name: The Carolina Dining Room
dining.must_know: At Pinehurst Resort. Fine dining. The traditional post-round dinner spot since 1901.

dining.name: The Deuce at Pinehurst
dining.must_know: Casual pub at the resort. Named after No. 2. Good post-round spot.

dining.name: Dugan's Pub
dining.must_know: Downtown Southern Pines. Sports bar with character. Locals' favorite.

insider_tips: No. 2 gets all the press, but No. 4 (Gil Hanse) might be the more enjoyable round. Play both.
Tobacco Road is either the best or worst round of your life. There is no middle ground. Play it.
Book a Pinehurst resort package for 3+ rounds — the per-round price drops significantly.
Walking is strongly encouraged at Pinehurst. Get a caddie for No. 2 — they know the green contours you can't see.
Mid Pines is the hidden star. Recently restored to pristine Donald Ross condition at half the price of No. 2.
Spring and fall are perfect. Summer is doable but hot. Winter has the best rates.
destinations.kit_tagline: Play No. 2 with a caddie, survive Tobacco Road, and discover why Mid Pines might be the best Ross course you've never heard of.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-April hits the sweet spot between spring weather and pre-summer pricing, with azaleas in bloom and greens running fast.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: RDU to Pinehurst is 90 minutes. Use arrival day for settling in and range work before No. 2 tomorrow.
Book first available morning slot. You want fresh legs for No. 2 and a caddie who isn't burned out from earlier loops.
The Hanse design plays better in morning light when you can read the bunkering. Save afternoon for recovery or Tobacco Road if the group votes yes.
Play this polarizing Strantz design when energy is loose and the group can handle the chaos. Cart-only anyway, so afternoon heat matters less.
Early morning walk on a Ross restoration is the perfect sendoff. Still leaves time for lunch and RDU departure by 2pm.

recommended_lodging.name: Pinehurst Resort (Carolina Hotel)
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: You need to stay here to play No. 2. The convenience of walking to the first tee and having all resort courses accessible makes the premium worth it. Book a 3+ round package and the per-round discount offsets some of the hotel cost.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 90+ days out for No. 2 access and resort package pricing.

bonus_plays.name: The Carolina Dining Room
bonus_plays.why: Do this once on Night 2 after No. 2. It's the ceremonial post-round tradition since 1901 and the group will remember it. Skip it the other nights and save money at The Deuce.

bonus_plays.name: Dugan's Pub
bonus_plays.why: Downtown Southern Pines locals spot with actual character. Better than resort bars for the casual nights when you want beers and burgers without the resort pricing.

bonus_plays.name: Pinehurst No. 8
bonus_plays.why: If anyone's flight gets in early on Day 1, this Fazio course is walkable and keeps the rust off without burning energy before No. 2.

destinations.avoid_reason: Pennsylvania winter. Cold, many courses close.
destinations.why_go: Saucon Valley is a top-100 course that hosted the Senior Players Championship. Lehigh Valley has excellent public golf, a growing craft beer scene, and SteelStacks entertainment. Within driving distance of NYC, Philly, and NJ. The underrated Mid-Atlantic golf weekend.

top_courses.name: Saucon Valley CC (Old Course)
top_courses.must_know: Hosted US Senior Open, Senior Players Championship. Private but resort guests get access through Saucon Valley packages. Three courses on property — Old Course is the championship test.

top_courses.name: Steel Club
top_courses.must_know: Former Bethlehem Steel executive course. Good conditioning, interesting history. Solid value.

top_courses.name: Bethlehem Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Municipal course with hilly terrain. Walking-friendly. Great value for the quality.

top_courses.name: Olde Homestead Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: 18 min from Bethlehem in New Tripoli. Rolling farmland setting. Challenging and scenic.

hidden_gems.name: Whitetail Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: In Bath. Mountain views. Well-maintained. Under the radar.

hidden_gems.name: Woodstone Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Near Danielsville. Public access to a private-feel course.

lodging_options.name: Hotel & Casino at Wind Creek Bethlehem
lodging_options.note: Casino resort on former Bethlehem Steel site. Restaurants, entertainment. Great group base.

lodging_options.name: Sayre Mansion B&B
lodging_options.note: Historic mansion in downtown Bethlehem. Upscale B&B experience.

lodging_options.name: Homewood Suites / Courtyard
lodging_options.note: Standard chains. Central Lehigh Valley location.

dining.name: Apollo Grill
dining.must_know: Best restaurant in Bethlehem. Mediterranean-inspired. Great bar.

dining.name: The Bayou
dining.must_know: Cajun/Creole in Bethlehem. Fun vibe, solid food, strong drinks.

dining.name: Bonn Place Brewing
dining.must_know: Craft brewery in a converted funeral home. Unique atmosphere. Great beer.

insider_tips: Saucon Valley Old Course is worth the premium. Book through a resort package for best access.
SteelStacks is a converted Bethlehem Steel plant — now an arts/entertainment district. Cool evening activity.
Lehigh Valley is 75 min from NYC, 60 min from Philly. Easy driving distance for weekend trips.
Wind Creek Casino makes this a mini-Atlantic City without the seedy boardwalk.
Fall foliage (Oct) in the Lehigh Valley is beautiful. Book for peak color.

activities: Arrive ABE, check into Wind Creek

destinations.kit_tagline: Top-100 golf an hour from Philly, craft beer in a funeral home, and zero Atlantic City sleaze.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Early June hits ideal weather before peak summer heat and avoids Memorial Day weekend pricing.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: ABE is 15 min from courses. Get in, settle at Wind Creek, hit balls if time allows.
Book the Old Course early before greens firm up. Championship test requires fresh legs.
Former executive course is more forgiving than Saucon. Midmorning start lets the group sleep in.
Early tee at the farmland track. Done by noon, brunch at Bonn Place, afternoon flights work.

recommended_lodging.name: Hotel & Casino at Wind Creek Bethlehem
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Casino resort on the old steel site puts you in the center of everything. Restaurants and casino on property mean the group stays together. Better than splitting across chain hotels.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Book 45 days out. Weekends fill early with NYC/Philly drive-ins.

bonus_plays.name: Apollo Grill
bonus_plays.why: Best restaurant in Bethlehem. Mediterranean menu, solid bar. Take the group here night 2 after Saucon Valley.

bonus_plays.name: Bonn Place Brewing
bonus_plays.why: Craft brewery in a converted funeral home. The setting alone is worth it. Great beer, casual food.

bonus_plays.name: SteelStacks
bonus_plays.why: Converted Bethlehem Steel plant with concerts and events. Cool industrial vibe. Check the calendar before you book.

bonus_plays.name: Bethlehem Golf Club
bonus_plays.why: Muni course 10 min from Wind Creek. If someone wants extra holes on day 1 or 3, $35 gets you walking-friendly terrain.

destinations.avoid_reason: Michigan winter shuts courses down. Most close by mid-October.
destinations.why_go: Northern Michigan is America's best-kept golf secret. World-class courses through cherry orchards and rolling dunes, plus a legit food and wine scene. Think Napa meets links golf.

top_courses.name: Arcadia Bluffs (Bluffs Course)
top_courses.must_know: Perched 200 feet above Lake Michigan. Links-style with ocean-like views. One of the most visually stunning courses in America.
signature_holes: #12 par-3 cliff edge over Lake Michigan

top_courses.name: Arcadia Bluffs (South Course)
top_courses.must_know: Reversible course inspired by Old MacDonald. Walking only with caddies. Unique throwback experience.

top_courses.name: LochenHeath Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Stunning East Grand Traverse Bay views. Well-conditioned, walkable, and excellent value for the quality.

top_courses.name: The Bear at Grand Traverse Resort
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design that will test every club in your bag. Elevation changes and tight fairways. Bring extra balls.

top_courses.name: Manitou Passage Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Great value course carved through Northern Michigan forest. Fewer crowds, quick rounds, solid conditions.

hidden_gems.name: Kingsley Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Private club that occasionally opens for public play. Walking-only, minimalist design. Call ahead for availability.

hidden_gems.name: Mistwood Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Incredible value for Northern Michigan. Well-maintained, fun layout, rarely crowded.

lodging_options.name: Grand Traverse Resort & Spa
lodging_options.note: Three courses on property including The Bear. Full resort amenities, spa, pool, restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Arcadia Bluffs Lodge
lodging_options.note: Stay on-site at Arcadia Bluffs. Boutique lodge with lake views and excellent dining.

lodging_options.name: Traverse City lakefront rental
lodging_options.note: Old Mission Peninsula or East Bay for wine tasting proximity. Book early for summer.

dining.name: The Cooks' House
dining.group_note: Best restaurant in TC. Small plates, local sourcing. Reserve well ahead for groups.

dining.name: Trattoria Stella
dining.group_note: Set in an old psychiatric hospital basement — sounds weird, tastes incredible. Great wine list.

dining.name: Sleder's Family Tavern
dining.group_note: Oldest restaurant in TC. Burgers and beer, taxidermy everywhere. Classic post-round spot.

dining.name: Bubba's
dining.group_note: Waterfront patio on West Bay. Casual eats, great sunset views, big group friendly.

non_golf_activities: Old Mission Peninsula wine tour (15+ wineries)
Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore hike
Brewery tour (Right Brain, Rare Bird, Workshop)
insider_tips: Arcadia Bluffs is 45 min southwest — worth every minute of the drive
Old Mission Peninsula wineries are casual and fun, not pretentious
Summer weekends book up months ahead — midweek is half the price
The Bear is a beast — play it when you're fresh, not day 3
Cherry season (mid-July) adds a fun local vibe but book lodging early
Sunset at Sleeping Bear Dunes is a must-do non-golf evening

items.title: Arrive TVC, pick up rental cars
Old Mission Peninsula wine tour (3 wineries)
The Bear at Grand Traverse Resort
Sleder's Family Tavern + downtown bar walk

destinations.kit_tagline: Links golf above Lake Michigan, cherry orchards between holes, and a wine scene that actually delivers.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-June hits the sweet spot before cherry season crowds and peak summer pricing kick in.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: TVC arrival day. Save legs for Arcadia tomorrow and hit Old Mission wineries while fresh.
Early start puts you on the bluffs before afternoon wind picks up off Lake Michigan.

recommended_itinerary.course_id: The Bear at Grand Traverse Resort
recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Play The Bear when you're fresh and the group's still sharp. This course doesn't forgive tired swings.
Early morning round leaves time for brewery stops before afternoon flights out of TVC.

recommended_lodging.name: Traverse City lakefront rental
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Four-bedroom on Old Mission Peninsula or East Bay puts you between courses and wineries. Kitchen saves money on breakfasts and lets you control the morning chaos.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 3-4 months out for June dates

bonus_plays.name: Mistwood Golf Course
bonus_plays.why: Day 3 afternoon if the group has legs left. Thirty-nine bucks for nine holes and you'll have the place to yourselves.

bonus_plays.name: Bubba's
bonus_plays.why: West Bay waterfront patio handles big groups without reservations. Sunset views are better than the food, but that's the point.

bonus_plays.name: Sleeping Bear Dunes sunset
bonus_plays.why: Twenty-minute drive from town. Climb the dune, watch the sun drop into Lake Michigan, skip rocks on the way down.

bonus_plays.name: Right Brain Brewery
bonus_plays.why: Downtown TC. Weird beer names, solid pours, walking distance to three other breweries if the group splits up.

destinations.nearest_airport: SAF (Santa Fe Regional) or ABQ (Albuquerque Sunport)
destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 10-20 min from SAF, 60-70 min from ABQ
destinations.avoid_reason: High desert winter can bring snow and freezing temps. Many courses close or go dormant.
destinations.why_go: Golf at 7,000 feet elevation with stunning high-desert scenery. Santa Fe's world-class art, cuisine, and culture make it the most interesting non-golf city on any golf trip list.

top_courses.name: Black Mesa Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Baxter Spann design set against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. Desert arroyos and juniper-lined fairways. Ball flies 10% farther at altitude.

top_courses.name: Towa Golf Resort (Buffalo Thunder)
top_courses.must_know: Hale Irwin design on Pojoaque Pueblo land. Casino resort on-site. Great value with stay-and-play packages.

top_courses.name: Paa-Ko Ridge Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: 27 holes carved through juniper and piñon at 6,500 feet. Panoramic Sandia Mountain views. Consistently rated top public course in NM.

top_courses.name: Marty Sanchez Links de Santa Fe
top_courses.must_know: City-owned links with stunning mountain views. Best muni value in New Mexico. Par-3 course on-site too for arrival day.

hidden_gems.name: Sierra del Rio Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: In Elephant Butte, worth the drive for the price. River views and zero crowds.

hidden_gems.name: Cochiti Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Robert Trent Jones Jr. design on Cochiti Pueblo. Incredible value for the pedigree. 40 min from Santa Fe.

lodging_options.name: Buffalo Thunder Resort & Casino
lodging_options.note: On-site golf at Towa. Casino, spa, pool. 15 min north of downtown Santa Fe.

lodging_options.name: La Fonda on the Plaza
lodging_options.note: Historic hotel right on the Santa Fe Plaza. Rooftop bar with mountain views. Best location in town.

lodging_options.name: Santa Fe adobe casita
lodging_options.note: Adobe-style homes near Canyon Road or the Railyard District. Private courtyards and kiva fireplaces.

dining.name: The Shed
dining.group_note: Iconic red and green chile. Always a line — go at 11am or call ahead for groups.

dining.name: Geronimo
dining.group_note: Canyon Road landmark. Elk tenderloin is legendary. Reserve 2+ weeks for groups.

dining.name: Tomasita's
dining.group_note: Locals' favorite for enchiladas and margaritas. Big portions, fun atmosphere.

dining.name: Kakawa Chocolate House
dining.group_note: Historic drinking chocolates. Perfect afternoon stop between rounds.

non_golf_activities: Canyon Road art gallery walk (80+ galleries)
Santa Fe Plaza and Palace of the Governors
Spa day at Ten Thousand Waves (Japanese-style)
insider_tips: Ball flies 10-15% farther at 7,000 feet — club down and enjoy it
Paa-Ko Ridge is 30 min east but the best golf in the area by far
Green chile is on everything and should be on everything
ABQ airport is cheaper to fly into but adds an hour drive each way
Indian Market weekend (August) is incredible but book 6+ months ahead
Meow Wolf is worth it even if you think you won't like art

items.title: Arrive ABQ, drive to Santa Fe

destinations.kit_tagline: Championship golf at 7,000 feet plus the best non-golf city you'll find on any trip itinerary.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-May hits peak spring conditions before summer heat and monsoon season starts in July.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most flights land after noon. Use afternoon for Canyon Road gallery walk and acclimation to 7,000 feet.
Start with the best course while legs are fresh. Morning tee before afternoon winds pick up in the high desert.
Second round after bodies are acclimated to elevation. Mountain backdrop views are best in morning light.

recommended_itinerary.course_id: Marty Sanchez Links de Santa Fe
recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Early tee on the muni gives time for checkout and ABQ airport drive. Easier track works for last-day legs.

recommended_lodging.name: Santa Fe adobe casita
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: For 6-8 guys, a house with kitchen and courtyard costs less than resort rooms and puts you walking distance to downtown restaurants. Breakfast and post-round beers at the house save $20/person/day easy.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 2-3 months out for prime locations near Plaza or Railyard

bonus_plays.name: The Shed at 11am sharp
bonus_plays.why: The line gets brutal after noon. Red chile enchiladas are the move. This is the one Santa Fe meal you cannot skip.

bonus_plays.name: Meow Wolf between rounds
bonus_plays.why: Takes 90 minutes and works even if your group thinks immersive art sounds ridiculous. Everyone leaves impressed.

bonus_plays.name: La Fonda rooftop bar at sunset
bonus_plays.why: Best view in Santa Fe. Margaritas and Sangre de Cristo mountain backdrop. Right on the Plaza so you can walk to dinner after.

bonus_plays.name: Marty Sanchez par-3 course
bonus_plays.why: City muni has a separate par-3 track. Perfect for arrival day or as a pre-dinner putting contest with beers.
bonus_plays.when: Day 1 late afternoon if energy allows

destinations.avoid_reason: Brutal heat and humidity. Afternoon thunderstorms common. Greens fees drop but conditions suffer.
destinations.why_go: The quieter, more upscale alternative to Myrtle Beach. World-class Lowcountry courses without the tourist madness. Caledonia and True Blue alone are worth the trip.

top_courses.name: Caledonia Golf & Fish Club
top_courses.must_know: Live oaks draped in Spanish moss frame the approach to the clubhouse. Consistently top 50 public in the US. The most beautiful golf experience on the Grand Strand.

top_courses.name: True Blue Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Caledonia's bold sister course. Massive greens, wide fairways, dramatic bunkering. Same Strantz magic, different personality.

top_courses.name: Pawleys Plantation Golf & Country Club
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus Lowcountry design through saltwater marsh. Gators on course are part of the charm.

top_courses.name: Heritage Club
top_courses.must_know: Ruins of an old rice plantation on the course. Beautiful setting through live oaks and along the Waccamaw River.

top_courses.name: Litchfield Country Club
top_courses.must_know: Willard Byrd classic. Tight tree-lined fairways. Not flashy but great value and solid conditions.

hidden_gems.name: River Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Tom Fazio design that flies under the radar. Excellent conditions for the price.

hidden_gems.name: Willbrook Plantation
hidden_gems.must_know: Dan Maples design through former rice plantation. Peaceful, scenic, and usually uncrowded.

lodging_options.name: Litchfield Beach & Golf Resort
lodging_options.note: Central location to all Pawleys courses. Condos and villas work well for groups. Pool and beach access.

lodging_options.name: Pawleys Plantation Resort
lodging_options.note: On-site Nicklaus course. Villas with golf views. Quiet and well-maintained.

lodging_options.name: Pawleys Island beach house
lodging_options.note: The island itself is tiny and exclusive. Litchfield area has more rental options and is closer to courses.

dining.name: Frank's Restaurant & Bar
dining.group_note: Best restaurant in the Pawleys area. Lowcountry fine dining. Reserve early for groups of 6+.

dining.name: Bistro 217
dining.group_note: Chef-driven menu that changes seasonally. Intimate but can handle groups with notice.

dining.name: Rustic Table
dining.group_note: Craft beer and elevated comfort food. Relaxed post-round atmosphere.

dining.name: Lee's Inlet Kitchen
dining.group_note: Cash only, been here since 1948. She-crab soup and fried seafood platters. No frills, all flavor.

non_golf_activities: Pawleys Island beach and hammock shops
Kayaking in the salt marsh creeks
Georgetown historic district and harbor walk
Deep-sea fishing charter out of Murrells Inlet
insider_tips: Play Caledonia first — it sets the tone for the entire trip
Book Caledonia + True Blue combo packages for 20-30% savings
Pawleys is only 25 min south of Myrtle but feels like a different world
Murrells Inlet Marshwalk is the best post-round dinner scene nearby
Spring rates (Mar-Apr) are peak but worth it for perfect conditions
Don't skip True Blue — it's bolder than Caledonia and just as memorable

items.title: Arrive MYR, drive to Pawleys Island

destinations.kit_tagline: Two Mike Strantz masterpieces wrapped in live oaks and Spanish moss, 25 minutes south of the Myrtle madness.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-March hits peak conditions before spring break crowds and captures 20-30% combo savings on Caledonia/True Blue.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Twilight rate gets the group on grass without rushing from MYR, and Byrd's tree-lined layout is forgiving for travel legs.
Play Caledonia first in morning light when the moss glows and before afternoon wind picks up off the marsh.
True Blue's massive greens and waste bunkers demand fresh legs and sharp eyes, so morning slot after a rest day from 36.
Early Nicklaus round through the marsh leaves time for checkout and 3-hour airport buffer before afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Litchfield Beach & Golf Resort
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Central to every course on the trip and the villa layout gives you pool, beach access, and kitchens for breakfast savings. Groups of 8-12 can book two adjacent units and stay under budget.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 6-8 weeks out for March dates and villa inventory

bonus_plays.name: Murrells Inlet Marshwalk
bonus_plays.why: Day 1 post-round seafood crawl across dockside restaurants. No reservations needed, everyone splits up and reconvenes with beers on the water.

bonus_plays.name: Frank's Restaurant & Bar
bonus_plays.why: Reserve for Day 2 after Caledonia. Best Lowcountry fine dining in the area and the group will be buzzing from the morning round.
bonus_plays.when: Day 2 evening, book 2-3 weeks ahead for parties of 8+

bonus_plays.name: Heritage Club back nine
bonus_plays.why: If the group wants a fifth round, Heritage's back nine through plantation ruins and along the Waccamaw is worth a twilight add on Day 3.

bonus_plays.name: Lee's Inlet Kitchen
bonus_plays.why: Cash-only seafood shack from 1948. She-crab soup and fried platters. Bring hundreds, leave smiling.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 75-90 min from TPA, 90 min from MCO
destinations.avoid_reason: Central Florida summer heat is oppressive. Afternoon thunderstorms guaranteed.
destinations.why_go: Three world-class courses in the middle of nowhere Florida. Reclaimed phosphate mines turned into rolling links-style terrain you'd never expect in the Sunshine State. Pure golf immersion — no distractions.

top_courses.name: Streamsong Red
top_courses.must_know: Coore/Crenshaw design with massive sand dunes and scrub. More walkable and strategic than Blue. The more 'thinking' course.

top_courses.name: Streamsong Blue
top_courses.must_know: Tom Doak design with dramatic elevation changes and bold features. Wider landing areas but more penal misses. The more visual course.
signature_holes: #7 par-3 over lake to hilltop green

top_courses.name: Streamsong Black
top_courses.must_know: Gil Hanse design (he did the Rio Olympics course). Newest of the three, most challenging. Deep bunkers and firm greens.

hidden_gems.name: Streamsong Chain of Lakes (par-3 course)
hidden_gems.must_know: Keith Rhebb-designed short course. Perfect warm-up or cool-down. Lit for night play.

hidden_gems.name: Southern Dunes Golf & Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Steve Smyers design 20 min from Streamsong. Surprisingly good and great value if you want a 4th round.

lodging_options.name: Streamsong Resort Lodge
lodging_options.note: Only lodging on property. Modern, clean, excellent dining. Stay-and-play is the way to do Streamsong.

lodging_options.name: Hotels in Lakeland
lodging_options.note: 30 min away if resort is booked or over budget. Loses the immersive feel but saves $100+/night.

dining.name: Restaurant Fifty-Nine
dining.group_note: Streamsong's flagship restaurant. Upscale Southern cuisine. The place for your big group dinner.

dining.name: P205
dining.group_note: Named for the phosphate compound. Craft cocktails and elevated pub fare. Great post-round.

dining.name: Bone Valley Tavern
dining.group_note: Casual grab-and-go near the golf courses. Quick bites between rounds.

dining.name: SottoTerra
dining.group_note: Underground wine cellar restaurant. Intimate setting, excellent pasta and wine selection.

insider_tips: Play all three courses — they're each completely different experiences
Walking with a caddie is the way Streamsong was designed to be played
Book the stay-and-play package for significant savings over à la carte
Red is most strategic, Blue is most dramatic, Black is most demanding
There's genuinely nothing around for 30+ miles — embrace the isolation
The par-3 course at night under the lights is a must-do
destinations.kit_tagline: Three top-100 courses carved from reclaimed mines in the middle of nowhere Florida. Golf purist heaven with zero distractions.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-February hits perfect Florida weather before spring break crowds drive up rates.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Arrival day from TPA gives you late afternoon for the short course under lights warm-up.
Blue's dramatic elevation changes play best in morning light, and you want fresh legs for Doak's biggest features.
Red's strategic routing rewards clear thinking, so morning tee time before anyone's tired or had too many at P205.
Black is the most demanding, so play it last when you're dialed in but still early enough to make afternoon flights.

recommended_lodging.name: Streamsong Resort Lodge
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Only option on property and the whole point of Streamsong is total immersion. Stay-and-play package pricing beats à la carte every time. Lakeland hotels save money but kill the vibe.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 8-10 weeks out for group blocks

bonus_plays.name: Restaurant Fifty-Nine
bonus_plays.why: Streamsong's flagship upscale Southern spot. Book the big group table for Day 3 after Red when everyone's settled in and ready for the proper celebration dinner.

bonus_plays.name: Chain of Lakes night round
bonus_plays.why: The par-3 course under the lights is legitimately fun and you already paid for it. Run it as a closest-to-the-pin contest with small stakes after dinner one night.

bonus_plays.name: P205
bonus_plays.why: Named for the phosphate formula and the best post-round spot. Craft cocktails are legit and the elevated pub food beats generic resort bar fare.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 60 min from MKE, 90 min from GRB
destinations.avoid_reason: Wisconsin winter closes courses. Snow from November through April most years.
destinations.why_go: Home of Whistling Straits and Blackwolf Run — two of America's best public golf facilities. The 2021 Ryder Cup put it on every golfer's bucket list. Kohler luxury wraps around world-class golf.

top_courses.name: Whistling Straits (Straits Course)
top_courses.must_know: 2021 Ryder Cup venue. Dramatic links course perched on Lake Michigan cliffs. Walking only with caddie required. Over 1,000 bunkers.

top_courses.name: Whistling Straits (Irish Course)
top_courses.must_know: The Straits' inland sibling. More rolling and less dramatic but still elite Pete Dye links-style golf.

top_courses.name: Blackwolf Run (River Course)
top_courses.must_know: Along the Sheboygan River. Hosted 2012 U.S. Women's Open. Tighter and more wooded than Whistling Straits.

top_courses.name: Blackwolf Run (Meadow Valleys Course)
top_courses.must_know: The most accessible of the four courses. Still Pete Dye character but more forgiving. Good warm-up round.

hidden_gems.name: The Bull at Pinehurst Farms
hidden_gems.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design 15 min from Kohler. Surprisingly great course at a fraction of Whistling Straits price.

hidden_gems.name: Quit Qui Oc Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Fun public course in Elkhart Lake. Great warm-up or cool-down round. Road America nearby for racing fans.

lodging_options.name: The American Club
lodging_options.note: Five-star Kohler resort. Only Forbes Five Star hotel in the Midwest. On-site spa uses Kohler products.

lodging_options.name: Inn on Woodlake
lodging_options.note: More affordable Kohler property. Same access to courses and restaurants. Great for groups on a budget.

lodging_options.name: Sheboygan lakefront rental
lodging_options.note: Sheboygan is 10 min away. Lake Michigan frontage available. Good for larger groups.

dining.name: The Immigrant Restaurant
dining.group_note: Six themed dining rooms in The American Club. Wisconsin-inspired fine dining. Jacket suggested.

dining.name: River Wildlife
dining.group_note: Private rustic lodge in the woods. Prix-fixe menu, game meats. Unique and memorable group dinner.

dining.name: Horse & Plow
dining.group_note: Casual American Club pub. Brats, burgers, Wisconsin cheese curds. No reservation needed.

dining.name: Trattoria Stefano
dining.group_note: In Sheboygan. Local favorite Italian. House-made pasta, excellent wine list.

insider_tips: Whistling Straits walking-only policy means you need a caddie ($45-50 + tip)
Book the Straits course first, then build your trip — it sells out fast
Stay at Inn on Woodlake for same course access at half the American Club price
River Wildlife dinner is the most unique dining experience you'll have on any golf trip
Summer evenings are long — daylight until 8:30pm means twilight rounds are full 18s
Cheese curds at Horse & Plow are mandatory, not optional

items.title: Whistling Straits — Straits Course (walk with caddie)

destinations.kit_tagline: Walk the 2021 Ryder Cup grounds, play four Pete Dye courses, and eat your weight in Wisconsin cheese curds.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-June gives you 8:30pm sunlight for twilight rounds and avoids Memorial Day and July 4th pricing spikes.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most accessible of the four courses gives you a warm-up round after noon arrival from MKE without the pressure of Straits or River.
Book the Straits first and build your trip around it. Morning start beats Lake Michigan wind and afternoon fatigue on a walking-only course.
Tighter and more wooded than Whistling Straits means morning gives you better ball flight visibility through tree corridors.
36-hole day works here because Irish is less demanding than Straits. Summer daylight until 8:30pm means you finish all 18.
Early Nicklaus round 15 minutes from Kohler gets you to MKE by 1pm for afternoon flights. Costs a third of another Whistling Straits round.

recommended_lodging.name: Inn on Woodlake
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Same tee time access as The American Club at half the price. Your group cares about the golf, not Forbes Five Star sheets. Save $600+ per person over three nights and put it toward another round.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Moderate · 6-8 weeks out. Book after you lock Straits tee times.

bonus_plays.name: River Wildlife
bonus_plays.why: Private rustic lodge in the woods with prix-fixe game meat menu. Most unique dining experience you'll have on any golf trip. Book when you book Straits tee times.

bonus_plays.name: Horse & Plow
bonus_plays.why: Cheese curds at Horse & Plow are mandatory, not optional. No reservation needed, walk in after any round.

bonus_plays.name: Kohler Design Center tour
bonus_plays.why: Free 30-minute walk through the factory that makes your toilet. Oddly fascinating and gives your legs a break between rounds.

destinations.nearest_airport: MSN (Dane County, Madison) or CWA (Central Wisconsin, Wausau)
destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 60-75 min from CWA, 90 min from MSN
destinations.avoid_reason: Central Wisconsin winter closes everything. Courses open mid-April to late October.
destinations.why_go: The Bandon Dunes of the Midwest. Multiple world-class courses on dramatic sandy terrain you'd never expect in Wisconsin. Pure golf immersion with zero pretension.

top_courses.name: Sand Valley Course
top_courses.must_know: Ben Crenshaw & Bill Coore design through ancient sand dunes. Walking only. Feels like Scottish links dropped into the Midwest.

top_courses.name: Mammoth Dunes
top_courses.must_know: David McLay Kidd design with the widest fairways you've ever seen. More fun and forgiving than Sand Valley. Everyone's favorite.

top_courses.name: The Lido
top_courses.must_know: Faithful recreation of the legendary lost Lido Golf Club. Tom Doak design. Newest course, already ranked top 10 in the US.

top_courses.name: Sedge Valley (par-3 course)
top_courses.must_know: 17-hole par-3 course perfect for arrival day. Walk-up play, no tee times. Views rival the big courses.

hidden_gems.name: SentryWorld
hidden_gems.must_know: In Stevens Point, 30 min away. Robert Trent Jones Jr. redesign. The flower hole (#16) is world-famous. Incredible standalone course.

hidden_gems.name: Lake Arrowhead (Lakes & Pines)
hidden_gems.must_know: Two solid courses in Nekoosa, near Sand Valley. Great value for extra rounds.

lodging_options.name: Sand Valley Resort Lodge & Cottages
lodging_options.note: On-site lodging with lodge rooms and cottages. Stay-and-play is the only way to guarantee Lido tee times.

lodging_options.name: Craig's Cabin or private homes
lodging_options.note: Multi-bedroom cabins on property. Perfect for groups who want their own space.

lodging_options.name: Hotels in Wisconsin Rapids
lodging_options.note: 20 min away. Budget option if resort is full. Limited dining/nightlife.

dining.name: Craig's Porch
dining.group_note: Sand Valley's signature restaurant. Farm-to-table with Wisconsin sourcing. Best dining on property.

dining.name: Mammoth Bar
dining.group_note: Casual post-round gathering spot. Great burgers and Wisconsin craft beers on tap.

dining.name: The Sandbox
dining.group_note: Grab-and-go food by the par-3 course. Quick bites between rounds.

dining.name: Camp Fire
dining.group_note: Outdoor fire pit dining. S'mores and stargazing. Great group bonding experience.

non_golf_activities: Hiking trails through the sand barrens
insider_tips: The Lido is the hardest tee time to get — book as early as possible
Mammoth Dunes is the crowd favorite and most fun for mixed-handicap groups
Walking only means you need to be reasonably fit or hire a caddie
Sedge Valley par-3 on arrival day is the perfect trip starter
Summer days are long (daylight until 9pm) — take advantage with late rounds
There is nothing around — embrace it. This is a golf monastery.

items.title: Arrive MSN, drive to Sand Valley

destinations.kit_tagline: Three Tom Doak-caliber courses dropped in ancient dunes an hour from nowhere—the Midwest's answer to links golf.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-June hits the sweet spot: courses in peak condition, daylight until 9pm for twilight rounds, pricing before July weekend premiums.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Walk-up par-3 course after midday flight arrival. Legs are fresh, stakes are low, everyone loosens up before the big courses.
Start with the crowd favorite while everyone's fresh. Wide fairways and forgiving design mean the whole group stays together and enjoys it.
Coore & Crenshaw's original design demands focus. Morning round before afternoon wind picks up—this course plays harder as the day goes on.
Save the crown jewel for last. Early tee time means you finish by noon with time to shower, debrief, and make afternoon flights out of MSN.

recommended_lodging.name: Sand Valley Resort Lodge & Cottages
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Stay-and-play is the only way to lock Lido tee times without praying to the golf gods. Cottages give you your own space for post-round decompression and card games. On-site means you roll out of bed onto the first tee.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 4-6 months out for Lido access

bonus_plays.name: Craig's Porch
bonus_plays.why: Farm-to-table Wisconsin sourcing, best dining on property. Book it for night one and night three—arrival celebration and Lido victory lap.

bonus_plays.name: Mammoth Bar
bonus_plays.why: Post-Mammoth Dunes is the right time for Wisconsin craft beers and burgers. Low-key, high-energy. Where everyone recaps the round and the lies get bigger.

bonus_plays.name: Camp Fire s'mores + stargazing
bonus_plays.why: Zero light pollution means you see stars you forgot existed. Outdoor fire pit, s'mores, whiskey. This is the bonding moment your group remembers most.

bonus_plays.name: Sedge Valley sunset loop
bonus_plays.why: If your Day 3 afternoon is open and someone's itching to hit more shots, the par-3 course at golden hour is the move. Walk-up, no pressure, pure fun.

destinations.avoid_reason: 120°F+ desert heat makes golf unbearable. Courses offer insanely cheap rates but it's brutal.
destinations.why_go: 100+ courses in the Coachella Valley with year-round sunshine. Mid-century cool vibe, incredible restaurants, pool culture, and some of the best value golf in the Southwest.

top_courses.name: PGA West (Stadium Course)
top_courses.must_know: Pete Dye's infamous design. 'Alcatraz' island green on #17 is iconic. The hardest public course in the valley — bring your A-game and extra balls.

top_courses.name: Indian Wells Golf Resort (Celebrity Course)
top_courses.must_know: Clive Clark design with stunning mountain backdrop. Well-maintained, fair test. Adjacent to the Tennis Garden.

top_courses.name: SilverRock Resort
top_courses.must_know: Arnold Palmer design surrounded by mountains. Former home of PGA Tour event. Great value for the pedigree.

top_courses.name: Escena Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design with wide fairways and mountain views. One of the best values in the valley. Great for all skill levels.

hidden_gems.name: Desert Willow (Firecliff Course)
hidden_gems.must_know: City-owned course that plays like a premium resort. Firecliff is the tougher of two courses. Incredible value.

hidden_gems.name: Tahquitz Creek (Legend Course)
hidden_gems.must_know: Budget-friendly Arnold Palmer design. Downtown Palm Springs location. Perfect arrival day round.

lodging_options.name: Hyatt Regency Indian Wells
lodging_options.note: On-site at Indian Wells Golf Resort. Two pools, spa, multiple restaurants. Great group hub.

lodging_options.name: La Quinta Resort & Club
lodging_options.note: Adjacent to PGA West. Casitas with private pools. Spanish colonial charm.

lodging_options.name: Palm Springs mid-century modern home
lodging_options.note: The desert is Airbnb paradise. Pool homes everywhere. Mid-century architecture is the vibe.

dining.name: Workshop Kitchen + Bar
dining.group_note: Industrial-chic in downtown PS. Best restaurant in the valley. Communal tables work for groups.

dining.name: El Jefe
dining.group_note: At the Saguaro hotel. Outdoor patio with pool views. Tacos and margaritas.

dining.name: King's Highway
dining.group_note: Retro diner at Ace Hotel. Great brunch and casual dinner. Cool mid-century vibe.

dining.name: Lulu California Bistro
dining.group_note: Downtown PS rooftop dining. Mountain views, creative menu, great cocktails.

non_golf_activities: Joshua Tree National Park day trip
Pool day at the Saguaro or Ace Hotel
Palm Canyon Drive shopping and galleries
insider_tips: Summer rates (Jun-Sep) drop 60-70% — playable before 8am if you can handle the heat
GolfNow and tee time apps have incredible same-day deals in the valley
Pool homes on Airbnb are the move for groups of 8+
PGA West Stadium is brutal — save it for when the group is playing well
Desert Willow is the locals' secret for best course/value ratio
Wind picks up most afternoons — morning rounds play calmer and cooler

items.title: El Jefe tacos + downtown PS bar crawl

destinations.kit_tagline: Desert golf under mountain backdrop, mid-century pool culture, and courses designed by every architect that matters.

default_recommended_dates.reason: Mid-February hits the sweet spot — 75°F mornings, prime conditions, and a week after Super Bowl chaos clears.

recommended_itinerary.tee_time_logic: Most flights land midday — use afternoon for range session and pool time instead of rushing a round.
Start with the locals' secret before wind picks up — best value in the valley and gets everyone dialed in.
Tackle the valley's hardest track when the group is warmed up — Alcatraz and San Andreas Fault demand morning calm.
Clive Clark design with mountain backdrop for the victory lap — fair test, great conditions, early enough to make afternoon flights.
Checkout and depart — PSP is 15 minutes from anywhere, easy exit.

recommended_lodging.name: Palm Springs mid-century modern home
recommended_lodging.why_this_one: Pool homes are the valley's unlock for groups of 8+. Mid-century architecture, private pool for post-round hangs, and kitchen saves $20/person/day on breakfast. Split 10 ways, it's $50/night per person.
recommended_lodging.booking_priority: Critical · 8-10 weeks out for February — prime season books early.

bonus_plays.name: Escena twilight nine
bonus_plays.why: Nicklaus design for $25 twilight after Day 2's morning round — wide fairways, beginner-friendly, and you're done by sunset.

bonus_plays.name: El Jefe into downtown bar crawl
bonus_plays.why: Tacos and margaritas at the Saguaro, then walk Palm Canyon Drive. Retro neon bars and mid-century lounges everywhere.

bonus_plays.name: Pool-deck putting contest
bonus_plays.why: Set up a makeshift course around the Airbnb pool — beer holes, music, low-stakes chaos after arrival.

bonus_plays.name: Joshua Tree sunrise
bonus_plays.why: 45-minute drive east gets you into otherworldly desert at dawn — worth it if anyone wakes up early on Day 2.
